brief_summary:
Rationale Cardiac surgery via median sternotomy carries an elevated risk of postoperative complications and delayed functional recovery. Preoperative physical therapy aims to reduce the incidence and severity of postoperative adverse outcomes and to accelerate functional recovery. However, current evidence on prehabilitation is inconsistent due to methodological heterogeneity. This study addresses the limitations of previous studies in four ways. First, a validated preoperative prediction model is used to select patients at high risk of in-hospital postoperative complications and delayed functional recovery. Second, a Cardiopulmonary Exercise Test (CPET) is performed at baseline to guide safe and effective intensity prescription. Third, as different patient populations are expected to benefit from different training programs, the prehabilitation program is tailored to the surgical indication: patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) receive high-intensity interval training (HIIT), and patients undergoing aortic valve replacement (AVR) receive moderate continuous training. Fourth, physical activity and self-management are promoted by using a wearable physical activity monitor and Shared Decision-Making (SDM) to stimulate and track daily physical activity.

Primary Objective To investigate the feasibility of a personalized, procedure-specific prehabilitation program (four to six weeks) for high-risk patients scheduled for elective cardiac surgery via sternotomy, with respect to recruitment, adherence, drop-out, safety, and acceptance. The program consists of two physiotherapist-supervised group training sessions per week, promotion of physical activity, and unsupervised home-based exercise.

Secondary Objective To provide a preliminary evaluation of participant responses to the intervention, focusing on changes in cardiorespiratory fitness (WRpeak), peripheral muscle strength (1RM), inspiratory muscle strength (MIP), physical activity (time spent active per day), and health-related quality of life (SF-36).

Study design A prospective, single-center, longitudinal, mixed-methods pilot study conducted at Maastricht University Medical Center (MUMC+).

Study population High-risk patients (n=24), defined by EuroSCORE II, who are scheduled for elective cardiac surgery via sternotomy (CABG or AVR).

Main study parameters/endpoints The primary endpoint is the feasibility of the prehabilitation intervention with respect to recruitment, adherence, drop-out, safety, and acceptance.

Burden Participation involves a structured time commitment with clinic and home components. Total supervised clinic time is estimated at 11-15 hours, covering two baseline assessments, 8-12 training sessions, and the final evaluation and interview. Total time at home is estimated at 16.5-19 hours, covering daily diary completion and unsupervised home exercises. These ranges depend on the patient's time to surgery.

Risks and mitigation The risk of acute cardiac events during exercise is elevated in this high-risk population. This risk is mitigated by strict adherence to NVVC/MUMC+ absolute stop criteria, continuous medical supervision during all testing and training sessions, and individualized intensity prescription based on CPET. The risk is considered acceptable in relation to the scientific value of studying this specific high-risk cohort, which makes the study group-related.

Benefit and group relatedness Direct clinical benefit cannot be guaranteed, as this is a feasibility study. However, patients receive an intensive, personalized prehabilitation program that is designed to reduce the incidence and severity of postoperative adverse outcomes.

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to investigate the relationship of forward head posture with burnout and quality of life in patients with mechanical neck pain.

The main questions the study aims to answer are:

Is there a significant correlation between the severity of forward head posture (measured by Kinovea software) and psychological burnout (evaluated by the Maslach Burnout Inventory, MBI)?

How do different degrees of forward head posture impact pain intensity, pressure pain threshold, cervical proprioception, and cognitive function (assessed via MoCA and the CogniFit application)?

comparison groups:

Researchers will compare Group 1 (patients with a forward head posture angle from 40 to 45 degrees) to Group 2 (patients with a forward head posture angle from 45 to 50 degrees) to see if varying degrees of forward head posture lead to different levels of physical, cognitive, and psychological impairments.

Participants will:

Undergo posture assessment using Kinovea software to determine their forward head posture angle and be allocated into their respective study groups.

pain intensity and pressure pain threshold measured using the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) and pressure algometry.

Perform a cervical proprioception test using a pointer laser device.

Complete cognitive evaluations using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and the CogniFit digital application.

Fill out standardized questionnaire, the Maslach Burnout Inventory (MBI) ,to assess burnout .
primary_outcomes: burnout assessed using the Maslach Burnout inventory
title: Relationship of Forward Head Posture With Burnout and Quality of Life

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to examine the effectiveness of the Fathers and Babies intervention (FAB). FAB aims to improve the mental health of fathers and provide strategies that help fathers support the mental health of their female partner. FAB was adapted from Mothers and Babies (MB), an evidence-based perinatal depression prevention intervention. FAB can be delivered as a standalone intervention or can be delivered alongside MB as a dyadic intervention to both fathers and mothers. In this longitudinal randomized controlled trial (RCT), the investigators will examine the effectiveness and implementation of the FAB intervention. To do this, the investigators will partner with Home Visiting (HV) programs in the state of Illinois (IL) and Texas (TX). Home visitors will be randomized to receive (intervention) or not to receive (controls) the FAB training. Home visitors that are randomized to receive FAB training will be trained and implement FAB or FAB with MB.

The specific aims include:

1. To evaluate the effectiveness of FAB, delivered as a stand-alone intervention, in improving paternal mental health outcomes compared to a control group that does not receive the FAB intervention;
2. To evaluate the effectiveness of FAB, when delivered in conjunction with MB, in improving paternal and maternal mental health outcomes compared to a control group that does not receive the FAB or MB intervention.
3. To evaluate FAB implementation to inform future intervention delivery and scalability; the investigators will assess key implementation outcomes guided by the RE-AIM framework (feasibility, acceptability, barriers, facilitators, reach, adoption, implementation, and maintenance).
primary_outcomes: Mental Health Outcomes: Stress
Mental Health Outcome: Depression
Mental Health Outcome: Anxiety
title: Fathers and Babies (FAB) Research Study

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical study was to learn whether the design of a dental implant affects how the gums around it respond to treatment of peri-implant mucositis, an early and reversible inflammation of the soft tissue around a dental implant. The study included systemically healthy, non-smoking adults with one-piece implants (made as a single unit) or two-piece bone-level implants (with a separate connecting part above the implant). The main questions were whether inflammation-related proteins in the fluid around the implant (interleukin-1 beta, interleukin-10, matrix metalloproteinase-8, and tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinases-1), clinical signs of inflammation, and selected bacteria changed differently after treatment around one-piece and two-piece implants.

Researchers compared implants with healthy gums and implants with peri-implant mucositis for each implant design, and compared the treatment response of the two designs over 3 months. All participants had a gum and implant examination, including plaque, bleeding, and pocket depth measurements and an assessment of gum thickness around the implant, and gave small samples of fluid and plaque from around the implant using paper strips and paper points. Participants with peri-implant mucositis received professional cleaning of the implant with an ultrasonic device with plastic-capped tips, a single application of chlorhexidine gel, and personal oral hygiene instructions, and returned 1 and 3 months later for repeat examinations and sampling.
interventions: Nonsurgical Mechanical Debridement With 1% Chlorhexidine Gel

title: Inflammatory Biomarkers, Microbial Findings, and Clinical Characteristics Before and After Treatment of Peri-Implant Mucositis Around One-Piece and Two-Piece Dental Implants

brief_summary:
Intensive care unit-acquired weakness (ICU-AW) is a common complication of critical illness and can negatively affect recovery and long-term physical functioning. Early and reliable assessment of muscle strength is essential for detecting muscle weakness and monitoring changes during an intensive care unit (ICU) stay. However, conventional strength assessments, such as manual muscle testing, require voluntary muscle contractions, making them unsuitable for patients who are not yet cooperative and limiting the possibility of assessing muscle strength during the early stages of critical illness. Magnetic femoral nerve stimulation offers an alternative, non-volitional approach to assessing quadriceps muscle strength. Nevertheless, the reliability and validity of this technique in critically ill patients remain insufficiently established.

This prospective methodological study aims to investigate the reliability and convergent validity of quadriceps twitch force measurements obtained using magnetic femoral nerve stimulation in critically ill patients.

A total of 33 cooperative adult patients admitted to medical or surgical ICUs will be included. Participants will undergo repeated quadriceps twitch force assessments over two consecutive days, performed by two assessors. Measurements will be conducted using a custom-developed frame designed to facilitate standardized quadriceps strength assessment at the bedside. Both single and paired magnetic stimulation techniques will be evaluated.

The primary outcome is the intra-rater reliability of paired twitch force measurements. Secondary outcomes include the inter-rater reliability of paired twitch force measurements, the intra-rater and inter-rater reliability of single twitch force measurements, and the convergent validity of twitch force measurements assessed through their association with maximal voluntary contraction force and potentiated twitch force. Reliability and agreement will be evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients and complementary measurement error analyses.

Establishing these measurement properties could support objective, non-volitional muscle strength assessment in critically ill patients, including those unable to participate in conventional strength testing. This could facilitate early baseline strength assessment, longitudinal monitoring of muscle recovery, and the evaluation of interventions aimed at preventing or treating ICU-AW..
primary_outcomes: Intra-rater reliability of paired quadriceps twitch force measurements
title: Beyond Voluntary Effort: Reliability and Validity of Magnetic Femoral Nerve Stimulation for Assessing Quadriceps Strength in Critically Ill Patient

brief_summary:
Delirium is a sudden change in attention, thinking, and awareness that can occur after heart surgery. It may slow recovery and is associated with longer hospital stays and poorer health outcomes. Patients undergoing heart surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass, also known as a heart-lung machine, may experience changes in blood sugar levels and in the body's response to insulin around the time of surgery.

This study aims to investigate how fluctuations in blood sugar levels, known as glycemic variability, are related to postoperative delirium. It will also examine whether insulin resistance, a condition in which the body responds less effectively to insulin, helps explain this relationship.

The study will evaluate intranasal insulin, which is insulin administered through the nose to reach the brain. Researchers will assess its effects on blood sugar fluctuations, insulin resistance, and the occurrence of postoperative delirium in patients undergoing heart surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. The findings may help guide future approaches to protecting brain function and improving recovery after heart surgery.
primary_outcomes: Number and Proportion of Participants with Postoperative Delirium Assessed Using the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) Within 7 Days After Surgery
title: Mechanisms and Intervention Strategies of Perioperative Glycemic Variability on Postoperative Delirium

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate whether personalized intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS), a form of noninvasive transcranial magnetic stimulation, can safely improve cognitive function in people with cognitive impairment related to cerebral small vessel disease.

The study will enroll 160 adults aged 45-85 years with mild cognitive impairment or mild vascular dementia related to cerebral small vessel disease. Participants will be randomly assigned in equal numbers to receive active iTBS or sham stimulation. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) will be used to identify an individualized stimulation target in the left prefrontal cortex. Sham stimulation will mimic the treatment experience without delivering effective magnetic stimulation. Participants and outcome assessors will not know which treatment participants receive.

Treatment will last 24 weeks. Participants will receive four stimulation sessions per day for five consecutive days during the first week, followed by four sessions on one day each week during weeks 2-24. Cognitive assessments will be performed before treatment, during treatment, at the end of treatment, and three months after treatment ends. The main outcome is the change in Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score from baseline to week 24. Brain MRI, electroencephalography (EEG), and adverse event monitoring will be used to examine changes in brain function and treatment safety.

primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) Total Score at Week 24
title: Personalized Intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation for Cognitive Impairment Related to Cerebral Small Vessel Disease

brief_summary:
Elranatamab is an effective BCMA-targeting bispecific antibody for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM). However, implementation in routine practice remains challenging due to monitoring requirements during step-up dosing for cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), together with the long-term burden of infection prevention and immunoglobulin replacement. Delivery models across the NHS vary considerably, including inpatient, ambulatory, outpatient, and virtual ward step-up dosing approaches. Supportive-care practice also evolved following NHS commissioning of primary immunoglobulin replacement for selected patients with hypogammaglobulinaemia.

This study will evaluate real-world implementation of elranatamab across the NHS to identify approaches to safe, scalable, and equitable delivery. Primary objectives are to evaluate acute delivery pathways for CRS/ICANS management during step-up dosing and long-term infection management, including immunoglobulin replacement. Secondary objectives include assessment of healthcare resource utilisation, treatment delivery patterns, infection outcomes, and clinical outcomes across diverse healthcare and socioeconomic settings.

The study population will be RRMM patients receiving elranatamab through NHS funding or compassionate access programmes from 01/01/2024 till 31/12/2026. Patients treated within clinical trials will be excluded.

This national multicentre retrospective observational study will utilise the UKCHART research network, with 20 participating tertiary and district general hospitals. Variation in delivery pathways, toxicity management strategies, and supportive-care practices, together with changes in NHS immunoglobulin replacement policy, has created a natural experiment in elranatamab implementation. Approximately 400 patients are anticipated. There will be two retrospective data collection sweeps. The first will capture baseline characteristics, treatment history, delivery pathways, toxicity management, infection prevention strategies, healthcare resource utilisation, and early outcomes. The second, conducted around 12 months later, will provide longer-term follow-up including infection outcomes, immunoglobulin replacement utilisation, treatment patterns, subsequent therapies, and cumulative resource utilisation.

Analyses will evaluate delivery models, CRS/ICANS management strategies, serious infections requiring hospitalisation, intensive care admission or death, immunoglobulin replacement utilisation, hospital admissions, bed-day utilisation, and variation across healthcare settings and socioeconomic groups.

This study will generate one of the largest national real-world datasets on elranatamab implementation. Findings will inform optimisation of monitoring strategies and supportive-care delivery including infection prevention, to guide evidence-based NHS delivery models for elranatamab and other T-cell redirecting therapies.
lead_sponsor: The Royal Wolverhampton Hospitals NHS Trust
primary_outcomes: Incidence of early severe treatment-related toxicity during step-up dosing
Incidence of serious infection during treatment
title: RE-RITE: Real-world Evaluation of Response, Implementation and Toxicity of Elranatamab

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial will evaluate the effect of two vitamin D3 supplementation regimens, administered in addition to oral iron therapy, on hematological and iron status in children aged 6-60 months with confirmed iron deficiency anemia and vitamin D deficiency.

Eligible participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive oral elemental iron at 3 mg/kg/day plus either vitamin D3 2000 IU/day or vitamin D3 400 IU/day for 12 weeks.

The primary outcome will be the between-group difference in mean change in hemoglobin concentration from baseline to Week 12. Secondary outcomes will include changes in serum ferritin, serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, red blood cell indices, serum iron, total iron-binding capacity, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and exploratory serum hepcidin, as well as adherence and adverse events.

Participants will receive follow-up assessments at Weeks 2, 4, 8, and 12 to assess adherence, tolerability, adverse events, and concomitant treatments. Laboratory assessments are planned at baseline and Week 12.
primary_outcomes: Between-Group Difference in Mean Change in Hemoglobin Concentration
title: Effect of Vitamin D Supplementation Added to Iron Therapy in Children With Iron Deficiency Anemia

The rehabilitation program is performed for 90 days and includes two approximately 45-minute sessions per day, combining physical exercise, breathing exercises, and cervical-postural rehabilitation. The study evaluates changes in the apnea-hypopnea index, nocturnal oxygen saturation, sleep fragmentation, daytime sleepiness, quality of life, psychological symptoms, cardiovascular and respiratory parameters, body mass index, and cervical spine alignment.

brief_summary:
The need for a generally available product that can safely and effectively increase antiviral resilience in susceptible populations became highly relevant during the recent COVID pandemic. The value continues with the endemic influenza season, which is now joined by COVID and, in susceptible adults, respiratory syncytial virus. The investigators recently completed a NIH-funded U19 project examining the immune potentiating effects of Immulina supplementation on biomarkers associated with antiviral resilience. Results showed robust NK responses in a substantial minority of participants. Further work has shown that the active compounds in Immulina (Braun-type lipoproteins) may be susceptible to degradation under GI conditions that are typically found during digestion after a meal (such as locally elevated intestinal pancreatic lipase and surfactant levels in the post meal state). In the investigators initial study, no instruction was given about when to take the investigational product in relationship to a meal or any restrictions on fat content indicating a possible spectrum of intestinal chemical conditions that could have affected the bioactivity of Immulina in different members of the study cohort.

Because of the heterogeneous immune biomarker response in the investigators U19 study cohort, the investigators propose to explore the role of food presence when ingesting the supplement and its possible impact on the immunostimulatory properties of Immulina. The investigators will address this question by seeking to characterize and optimize the oral delivery of Immulina through evaluating product quality, bio accessibility, and stability under simulated GI conditions relevant to fasting and fed states. This will be accomplished through botanical authentication, bioassay-based standardization, and dissolution performance of the clinical encapsulated product to ensure consistency with previously characterized material. Additionally, investigators will perform in vitro studies to identify dietary conditions most likely to preserve Immulina activity. Further, an additional pharmacodynamic study will be performed with various Immulina doses over four weeks in individuals who will fast for 2 hours or have just completed a meal after taking daily dose of Immulina to compare the effects of fed vs 2 hr. fasting after ingesting Immulina on biomarkers of antiviral resilience. Finally, investigators will examine the effects of a 4-week pretreatment with Immulina vs. placebo on vaccine-specific antibody titers after routine influenza immunization by comparing vaccine-specific antibody titers immediately prior and 4 weeks after immunization.

These studies will allow optimal design of future clinical trial protocols to assess impact of daily Immulina on antiviral resilience in susceptible populations with or without known immune compromise due to concomitant disease (e.g. cancer, transplant, etc.) or age (e.g., immune senescence).
primary_outcomes: Changes in NK cell activity after ingesting Immulina for 4 Weeks
title: Effects of Food Intake on Biomarker Activity in Normal Humans Taking Immulina

brief_summary: This randomized study evaluated whether brief wrist vibrations delivered through an Apple Watch during algorithm-identified rapid eye movement (REM) sleep could reduce depressive symptoms over approximately four weeks. Adults with clinically significant depressive symptoms were assigned to either REM-contingent haptic stimulation or a monitoring-only control condition. Both groups used the same iPhone and Apple Watch applications and received the same morning Smart Alarm function; only the intervention group received night-time haptic stimulation during probable REM sleep. Sleep stages were estimated in real time using wrist accelerometry and photoplethysmography. Depressive symptoms were assessed using clinician-rated and self-reported measures, with the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) as the primary clinical outcome and the Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II) as a secondary outcome. Sleep architecture, treatment exposure, adherence, and tolerability were also evaluated.
interventions: Smartwatch Sleep Monitoring and Smart Alarm
primary_outcomes: Final Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) Score
title: REM Sleep Disruption and Its Potential Uses in Depression Management

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if daily oil pulling with coconut oil or sesame oil works as effectively as a standard mouthwash to treat gum swelling and redness (gingivitis) in adults aged 18 to 55 years. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does daily oil pulling with virgin coconut oil or sesame oil reduce dental plaque buildup as effectively as 0.2% chlorhexidine mouthwash over an 8-week period?
* Does oil pulling reduce gum inflammation, bleeding, and tongue coating while avoiding common mouthwash side effects such as tooth staining?
* Does oil pulling improve oral health-related quality of life and overall patient satisfaction? Researchers will compare three groups - participants using virgin coconut oil, participants using sesame oil, and participants using 0.2% chlorhexidine mouthwash - to evaluate changes in oral health over 8 weeks.

Participants will:

* Receive professional dental cleaning (scaling) and standardized toothbrushing instructions at the start of the study.
* Swish 10 mL of their assigned oil for 7 minutes once daily in the morning on an empty stomach, or rinse with 10 mL of chlorhexidine mouthwash for 1 minute at night, every day for 8 weeks (56 days).
* Visit the dental clinic at baseline (Day 0), week 4 (Day 28), and week 8 (Day 56) for clinical oral exams, salivary pH testing, and short surveys on comfort and satisfaction.

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn how well the SalivIQ™ Strep A test detects Group A Streptococcus, the bacteria that cause strep throat. The study will include children and adults with symptoms that may be caused by strep throat.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* How well does the SalivIQ™ Strep A test identify participants who have strep throat?
* How well does the SalivIQ™ Strep A test identify participants who do not have strep throat?
* How do results from saliva and throat swab samples tested with the SalivIQ™ Strep A test compare with standard laboratory testing?

Participants will:

* Provide a saliva sample.
* Have throat swab samples collected.
* Have samples tested using the SalivIQ™ Strep A test and standard laboratory methods.

Researchers will compare the SalivIQ™ Strep A test results with standard laboratory test results to determine how accurately the test detects Group A Streptococcus. Participation in the study will not change the medical care participants receive based on their routine clinical testing.

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, multicenter, biomarker-guided Phase II study evaluating the efficacy and safety of hexaminolevulinate-mediated cervical photodynamic therapy (HAL-PDT) in women with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN3). Approximately 260 women aged 18 to 50 years with histologically confirmed CIN3 and a positive baseline human papillomavirus (HPV) test will be enrolled.

Participants will receive HAL-PDT using a 5% hexaminolevulinate ointment and a light fluence of 125 J/cm². Treatment will be administered once every 2 weeks for a total of 6 treatments.

The primary objective is to evaluate the overall efficacy of HAL-PDT, measured by the pathological regression rate at 6 months after the first treatment. Pathological regression is defined as biopsy findings showing normal cervical tissue or low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL/CIN1).

The study will also evaluate pathological regression at 12 months, HPV clearance at 3, 6, and 12 months, treatment-related adverse events, changes in cervical lesion characteristics, and the associations between HPV integration status and treatment response. Cervical exfoliated-cell methylation status and p16/Ki-67 dual-stain status will also be assessed during follow-up.
primary_outcomes: Pathological Regression Rate at 6 Months
title: Exploratory Study of the Efficacy of HAL-PDT in CIN 3

brief_summary:
Preterm infants are babies born before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy. Early nutrition is important for their growth and development, and it may also be associated with how their heart develops and functions during infancy.

This prospective observational study aims to investigate the association between early nutritional exposure during the neonatal period and cardiac structure and function at 12 months of corrected age in preterm infants. The study will be conducted at Assiut University Hospital and El-Eman General Hospital in Assiut, Egypt.

Preterm infants born before 37 weeks of gestation who are admitted to the neonatal unit within 24 hours of birth, have adequate records of their nutritional intake, and whose parents provide written informed consent will be considered for participation. Infants with major congenital heart disease, known congenital cardiomyopathy, major genetic or chromosomal abnormalities, or other specified exclusion criteria will not be included.

The study will collect information about maternal and neonatal characteristics, neonatal complications, feeding patterns, growth, and anthropometric measurements. Cardiac structure and function will be assessed using echocardiography at birth, 6 months, and approximately 12 months of corrected age. Growth measurements will also be recorded at different time points, including 12 months of corrected age.

The study will compare cardiac measurements and growth outcomes among infants with different early nutritional exposures. It will also investigate which early nutritional and clinical factors are associated with left ventricular mass index at 12 months of corrected age.

The findings may improve understanding of the relationship between early nutrition and cardiovascular development in preterm infants. Participation will involve clinical data collection, growth measurements, and echocardiographic assessments, with written informed consent obtained from parents or legal guardians.
primary_outcomes: to investigate the association between early nutritional strategies and cardiac structure and function at 12 months of corrected age.
title: Early Nutrition and Heart Structure and Function in Preterm Infants During the First Year of Life

brief_summary: This study aimed to examine the relationship between nutrition education programs directed at mothers and food refusal observed in preschool children, maternal picky eating behaviors, and maternal feeding practices. The study was conducted in a public preschool institution affiliated with the Istanbul Provincial Directorate of National Education. The study sample consisted of 202 children aged 3-6 years attending the preschool where the study was carried out, and their mothers. Data were collected using a Sociodemographic Information Form, a Nutrition Habits Information Form, the Adult Picky Eating Scale, and the Child Food Refusal Scale. Participants were determined using purposive sampling and were randomly assigned to either an education group (n₁ = 101) or a control group (n₂ = 101). Pre-tests were administered to both groups at the beginning of the study. Following the pre-test, the education group received training on picky eating and food refusal once a week for four weeks, consisting of four sessions lasting 30-45 minutes each. No education or information was provided to the control group. Data collection tools were administered to both groups before and after the intervention.
primary_outcomes: Change in Child Food Refusal Scale Scores
title: Parent-Focused Nutrition and Feeding Education on Maternal Picky Eating and Food Refusal

brief_summary: Implant dentistry has become a fundamental aspect of modern dental practice, with its success now determined by more than just Osseo integration. Various factors play a critical role in the long-term success of dental implants, one of the most important being the stability of the peri-implant soft tissues, which are essential for maintaining both function and aesthetics. This study aims to compare the outcomes of sub epithelial connective tissue grafts and de-epithelialized connective tissue grafts in conjunction with delayed implant placement.
primary_outcomes: Gingival index
title: Evaluation of Different Grafting Technique of Thin Gingival Phenotype With Delayed Dental Implants

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether a modified (less frequent) dosing schedule of daratumumab, when added to standard VRd therapy, can be an effective induction regimen for treating newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does the modified (less frequent) daratumumab dosing regimen increase the rate of MRD (minimal residual disease) negativity after 4 cycles of induction therapy (as compared to standard VRd therapy)?
2. Is the modified less-frequent dosing schedule safe and does it achieve adequate drug levels
3. What is the clinical response of patients to the treatment?

Treatment regimen Daratumumab (Dara), Bortezomib, Lenalidomide, and Dexamethasone will be given together for four cycles of induction therapy

Duration of each cycle will be 28 days

1. Daratumumab will be given at standard dose of 16mg/kg - Day 1, 15, 29, 50, 71, and 92 (First three doses every 2 weeks, followed by the next three doses every 3 weeks). This will be given intravenously in saline
2. Bortezomib: 1.3 mg/m2 - Given once weekly subcutaneously (similar to insulin)
3. Lenalidomide: 15-25 mg orally for 21 days, followed by a 7-day gap.
4. Dexamethasone: 40mg given once weekly

Response Assessment

* Response assessment - A bone marrow test will be done within two weeks of end of cycle 4 in order to assess the cancer burden via a special test called MRD (minimal residual disease) in the bone marrow.
* Blood tests will be performed to assess your response to treatment (serum protein electrophoresis, immunofixation electrophoresis and serum free light chain assay) after cycle 2 (between day 51-day 56) and cycle 4 (between 107-112). These blood tests are routinely done for all myeloma patients during their treatment to assess response.
interventions: Daratumumab (Intravenously) with VRd (Bortezomib, Lenalidomide, and Dexamethasone)
primary_outcomes: Post-induction MRD negativity rate
title: Less Doses of Daratumumab Are Adequate to Achieve Response in Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma

brief_summary: This project aims to integrate the knowledge system of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) pattern differentiation with TCM knowledge, combining TCM principles with modern Western pharmacology to fundamentally understand the pathogenesis of chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN). It employs herbal fumigation and washing therapy for CIPN, offering novel treatment approaches to better guide and assist clinical practice.
lead_sponsor: Emeishan Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine
primary_outcomes: Patient Experience
CIPN Grading Criteria
Quality of Life Questionnaire QLQ-C30
Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale
title: A Study on the Clinical Efficacy of Fumigation and Washing With Modified Astragalus and Cinnamon Twig Decoction With Five Herbs in the Treatment of Post-Chemotherapy Peripheral Neuropathy

brief_summary:
This study will compare two ways of managing the hernia sac during laparoscopic surgery for an indirect inguinal hernia, a type of groin hernia. A hernia sac is a pouch of tissue that extends through the hernia opening. In the standard technique, the sac is fully separated from nearby structures and returned to the abdomen. In the alternative technique, called Primary Abandon of the Sac (PAS), the lower part of the sac is left in place to reduce the amount of tissue dissection. Both techniques use mesh to repair the hernia.

The main question is whether leaving the lower part of the sac in place results in an acceptably similar rate of seroma compared with the standard technique. A seroma is a collection of fluid near the area where surgery was performed. The study will also compare operation time, pain, quality of life, complications, return to daily activities, and whether the hernia comes back.

The study plans to enroll 90 adults with a primary indirect inguinal hernia on one side who are scheduled for elective laparoscopic repair. Participants will be assigned by chance to one of the two surgical techniques, with an equal chance of receiving either technique. Participants and the researchers assessing their recovery will not know which technique was used; the operating surgeon will know.

Participants will have follow-up assessments at 1 day, 7 days, 1 month, 6 months, and 12 months after surgery. The main assessment of seroma will take place 30 days after surgery.
interventions: Standard TAPP Repair With Complete Hernia Sac Dissection
TAPP Repair With Primary Abandon of the Sac
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants With Seroma at Postoperative Day 30
title: Comparison of Two Surgical Techniques for Indirect Inguinal Hernia Repair

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if topical application of crisaborole 2% ointment can treat flexural and/or genital psoriasis in adult patients of both genders. It will also learn about the safety of crisaborole 2% ointment.

The main questions it aims to answer is:

* Does crisaborole 2% ointment work effectively in flexural and/or genital psoriasis in adults?
* is crisaborole 2% ointment well tolerated in flexural and/or genital psoriasis in adults?
* Is crisaborole 2% ointment comparable to tacrolimus 0.1% ointment in terms of efficacy and safety in flexural and/or genital psoriasis in adults?

Researchers will compare crisaborole 2% ointment to tacrolimus 0.1% ointment to see if crisaborole works as effective and is as well-tolerated.

Participants will:

* apply topical crisaborole 2% ointment or tacrolimus 0.1% ointment twice daily for 6 weeks to plaques of flexural and/or genital psoriasis.
* Visit the clinic once every 2 weeks for checkups and photography.
* Keep a diary of their symptoms.
primary_outcomes: Target Lesion Severity Score (TLSS)
Static Physician's Global Assessment (sPGA)
Dynamic Physician Global Assessment (dPGA)
title: Efficacy of Crisaborole 2% Ointment Versus Tacrolimus 0.1% Ointment in the Treatment of Intertriginous and/or Anogenital Psoriasis: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Study.

brief_summary: This study is a prospective randomized controlled trial to assess the efficacy of erector spinae plane (ESP) blocks in patients undergoing autologous free flap breast reconstruction. Currently, patients undergoing this procedure remain in the hospital initially for flap monitoring until discharge criteria is met, when pain is adequately controlled and patient is able to ambulate independently. Prolonged hospital stays can occur due to persistent pain, typically abdominal pain as breasts are insensate following mastectomy. Persistent pain at abdominal incision can increase opioid requirements, impede ambulation trials, and delay discharge. This study aims to utilize ESP blocks to help augment pain control in patients undergoing autologous free flap breast reconstruction. The ESP block is a safe regional block that is already commonly utilized by multiple surgical specialties, such as general surgery, obstetrics and gynecology, cardiothoracic surgery, neurosurgery, and orthopedic surgery. The ESP block is an ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia technique where a local anesthetic is injected into the fascial plane between the erector spinae muscles and the thoracic vertebrae's transverse processes. This injection spreads longitudinally, blocking the spinal nerves and providing multi-dermatomal pain relief to the anterior, posterior, and lateral chest and abdominal walls, making it useful for surgeries and managing chronic pain. Patients in this study will be randomized into one of two groups, ESP block or No ESP (NESP) block group. The investigators will not be blinding patients to their study arm assignment, as this would require injecting placebo which the investigators believe would be an unnecessary risk to patient. Additionally, it was determined that it would not be feasible to blind patients as the ESP block participants would be numb in their abdomen and patients would immediately know whether or not they received the block. Participants will be informed of their study arm assignment on the day of surgery prior to proceeding to the operating room. Patients will then be asked to fill out a twice daily survey on pain and ambulation trials. Inpatient data on pain medication administration and time to discharge will be collected through chart review. This study aims to investigate the efficacy of ESP blocks to improve management of pain at abdominal incision, decrease inpatient opioid consumption, decrease time to ambulation, and decrease length of stay.
primary_outcomes: Inpatient pain control
title: ESP Blocks in Breast Free Flaps

brief_summary: This study will test BNT3219 (also known as PM1092) in adults with advanced solid tumors whose cancer has progressed after available standard treatments. It is the first study of BNT3219 in people, and it will test different dose levels to identify safe and tolerable doses. The study will also examine how the treatment moves through the body, whether the immune system reacts to them, and whether it shows signs of shrinking or controlling tumors.
primary_outcomes: Occurrence of dose-limiting toxicities (dose escalation only)

Number and percentage of participants with treatment emergent adverse events (TEAEs) by TEAEs by National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events grading, seriousness, and relatedness
Number and percentage of participants with dose interruptions, or discontinuations of study treatment due to TEAEs
Objective response rate (dose expansion only)
title: A First-in-human Clinical Trial to Test if the Investigational Drug BNT3219 is Safe and Potentially Beneficial for People With Advanced Solid Tumors When Given Alone or Together With Other Investigational Drugs

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to understand the feasibility and acceptability on a mindfulness-based intervention to address co-existing smartphone addiction and psychological distress among adolescents ages 13-19 self-reporting elevated levels of depression and/or anxiety symptoms and problematic digital phone use. The main questions it aims to answer are: (1) is Mindwire, a mindfulness-based intervention, feasible and acceptable in addressing co-existing smartphone addiction and psychological distress among adolescents; and (b) what are the mechanistic pathways, particularly the role of circadian rhythm, sleep quality, and emotion regulation, in phone use and psychological distress.

Participants will be in this research study for 3 months. After screening and onboarding, they will be asked to:

* participate in 18 days of the Mindwire program
* answer a 45-60 minute online survey immediately before, immediately after, and approximately six weeks after the Mindwire program
* participate in a 60-90 minute interview asking about their experience going through the program
primary_outcomes: Study Recruitment Feasibility as Measured by Participant Recruitment Rates
Study Retention Feasibility as Measured by Participant Retention Rates
Intervention Engagement Feasibility as Measured by Participant Engagement with Intervention
Intervention Acceptability as Measured by Client Satisfaction Questionnaire (CSQ-8)
Intervention Acceptability as Measured by Session Evaluation Form
title: The Mindful Smartphone Use Study

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to compare the effects of manual lymphatic drainage (MLD), intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC), and passive rest on recovery following exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) induced by a Nordic Hamstring Exercise protocol in physically active young adults.

Participants will be randomly allocated to one of three recovery strategies after completing a standardized eccentric exercise protocol designed to induce muscle damage. Recovery will be assessed through clinical, metabolic, functional, and anthropometric outcomes, including delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS), perceived recovery status (PRS), blood lactate concentration, countermovement jump (CMJ) performance, and thigh circumference. Assessments will be conducted at baseline, immediately after exercise, during the acute recovery period, immediately after the assigned intervention, and during follow-up visits at 24 hours, 3 days, and 7 days.

The study aims to provide evidence regarding the effectiveness of manual lymphatic drainage and pressotherapy as post-exercise recovery strategies in physically active young adults.
primary_outcomes: Change in Blood Lactate Concentration
Change in Countermovement Jump Performance
title: Effects of Manual Lymphatic Drainage and Pressotherapy on Muscle Recovery After Eccentric Exercise in Physically Active Young Adults

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to evaluate clinical, functional, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) outcomes after arthroscopic dynamic anterior stabilization using the long head of the biceps tendon (DAS-LHB) in patients with recurrent anterior glenohumeral instability.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How much does the Western Ontario Shoulder Instability Index (WOSI) change from before surgery to a minimum of 2 years after DAS-LHB?
* What is the structural integrity and healing status of the transferred long head of the biceps tendon on routine postoperative MRI obtained at least 6 months after surgery?
* What are the postoperative rates of recurrent instability, reoperation, residual apprehension, return to sport, and changes in shoulder function and range of motion?

Researchers will also compare patients who underwent isolated DAS-LHB with patients who underwent DAS-LHB combined with Hill-Sachs remplissage to explore whether the addition of remplissage is associated with differences in clinical, functional, and imaging outcomes. This comparison is exploratory and was not randomized.

Participants underwent surgery as part of routine clinical care and will not receive any additional treatment or imaging for research purposes. Researchers will review existing clinical records and imaging studies. If routine follow-up data are incomplete, some participants may be contacted by telephone, secure electronic questionnaire, or clinical review to complete standardized outcome assessment.
interventions: Arthroscopic Onlay Dynamic Anterior Stabilization Using the Long Head of the Biceps Tendon (DAS-LHB)
primary_outcomes: Change in Western Ontario Shoulder Instability Index (WOSI) score
title: Outcomes of Arthroscopic Dynamic Anterior Stabilization With and Without Remplissage

brief_summary:
This study is a multicenter 1:1 randomized controlled trial, enrolling patients with chronic neck pain from the Rehabilitation Medicine Department of Huizhou Third People's Hospital. A total of 60 participants are planned to be recruited, divided 1:1 into a trial group receiving the knot-release acupuncture method and a sham acupuncture control group. The study aims to evaluate the immediate clinical efficacy and safety of the knot-release acupuncture method for treating chronic neck pain and to explore its peripheral-to-central mechanisms using multimodal detection technologies. The research content includes:

1. Dynamically monitoring core evaluation indicators in enrolled patients, including VAS scores, real-time shear wave elastography (SWE), cervical range of motion (ROM), Neck Disability Index (NDI-TH), and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), to assess the immediate clinical efficacy and safety of the knot-release acupuncture method for chronic neck pain.
2. Observing and recording any adverse events throughout the intervention period, systematically and scientifically evaluating the clinical safety of the knot-release acupuncture method for chronic neck pain, and providing a safety basis for its standardized clinical application.
interventions: Untangling Needle Therapy: Acupuncture with Untangling Needle
primary_outcomes: Visual Analogue Scale（VAS）
Trapezius shear modulus measured by a soft tissue mechanical imager using real-time shear wave elastography (SWE) technology and 2D ultrasound qualitative imaging features
title: The Clinical Efficacy and Multimodal Imaging Mechanism of the Knot-tying Technique in the Treatment of Chronic Neck Pain

brief_summary:
This research is being done to study the safety and feasibility of implanting and retrieving a microdevice that releases microdoses of 20 specific drugs or drug combinations as a possible tool to evaluate the effectiveness of several cancer drugs against lung cancer or mesothelioma.

The name of the intervention(s) involved in this study are:

Implantable Microdevice (IMD) Surgery (excision of tumor) Drugs used in this study will include drugs already used as standard of care for the treatment of lung cancer and mesothelioma, or other drugs that are approved or being investigated for these indications.
primary_outcomes: Safety of microdevice implantation and indwelling
title: Implantable Microdevices for in Situ Evaluation of Drug Responses in Lung Cancer

brief_summary: This study aims to compare two impression techniques, the neutral zone technique and the admixed impression technique, for making complete dentures in patients with atrophic mandibular ridges (severely resorbed lower jaw ridges). A total of 60 patients aged 50-70 years will be included and divided into two groups of 30 patients each. One group will receive complete dentures made using the neutral zone technique, while the other group will receive complete dentures made using the admixed impression technique. Patient comfort during impression making will be assessed and compared between the two techniques to determine which technique provides greater comfort for patients with atrophic mandibular ridges.
conditions: Atrophic Mandibular Ridge in Edentulous Patients
primary_outcomes: Mean total patient comfort score during impression making
title: Comparison Between Neutral Zone and Admixed Impression Techniques for Atrophic Mandibular Ridges

brief_summary:
he purpose of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether virtual reality can reduce pain, anxiety, and physiological stress during chest tube removal in adult patients undergoing coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does virtual reality reduce pain intensity during chest tube removal?
* Does virtual reality reduce anxiety levels and stabilize vital signs? Researchers will compare patients receiving virtual reality with patients receiving routine care to determine whether virtual reality improves patient comfort during the procedure.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to a virtual reality group or a control group
* Have their pain, anxiety, and vital signs measured before the procedure
* Undergo chest tube removal with or without virtual reality
* Have their pain, anxiety, and vital signs measured again after the procedure
interventions: VR Shinecon G04EA Virtual Reality Headset
primary_outcomes: Pain Intensity (VAS)
title: VR During Chest Tube Removal After CABG

brief_summary: This study aims to develop and evaluate an innovative prehospital emergency transport system for patients with acute ischemic stroke to reduce delays in reperfusion treatment. The system integrates artificial intelligence-based prehospital stroke assessment, selected examinations and blood collection in the ambulance, and real-time information sharing between emergency medical services and the receiving hospital. Its effectiveness will be evaluated in a multicenter, stepped-wedge cluster randomized controlled trial comparing the innovative system with standard prehospital care. The primary outcome is the time from hospital arrival to intravenous thrombolysis.
interventions: Innovative pre-hospital emergency transport system for acute ischemic stroke
primary_outcomes: Door-to-Needle Time
title: Prehospital Response and Emergency Stroke Transport Optimisation

brief_summary: This study was conducted to investigate the effect of chewing gum during intravenous blood sampling on pain and anxiety levels in individuals.
interventions: Chewing gum was done during the intravenous blood draw procedure
primary_outcomes: pain level-Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
state anxiety level- state anxiety inventory(STAI-I)
title: The Effect of Chewing Gum on Pain and State Anxiety During Intravenous Blood Sampling

brief_summary: Endotracheal tube cuff pressure outside the recommended range of 20-30 cmH₂O is common in routine anesthesia practice. Over-inflation can injure the tracheal mucosa, while under-inflation increases the risk of aspiration and ventilator-associated pneumonia. This prospective, single-center, uncontrolled before-and-after study evaluates whether a brief educational intervention improves cuff pressure management in the operating room. Adult patients undergoing general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation at Marmara University Pendik Training and Research Hospital are enrolled in two consecutive periods. In both periods, cuff pressure is measured with a calibrated manometer shortly after intubation, together with the professional role and clinical experience of the provider who inflated the cuff. Between the two periods, a two-minute educational video explaining the importance of optimal cuff pressure and demonstrating manometer use is distributed to all operating room staff involved in cuff inflation, and reminder posters are placed in every operating room. The primary outcome is the proportion of cuff pressure measurements within the recommended range before versus after the intervention. The secondary outcome is the association between the cuff-inflating provider's role and experience and cuff pressure appropriateness. No change to patient care beyond the educational intervention is made.
interventions: Brief educational intervention (educational video and reminder posters)
lead_sponsor: Marmara University Pendik Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients with endotracheal tube cuff pressure within the recommended range (20-30 cmH₂O)
title: Effect of a Brief Educational Intervention on Endotracheal Tube Cuff Pressure

brief_summary:
This prospective, randomized controlled trial aims to compare the effects of two different kinesio taping techniques on pain, shoulder function, acromiohumeral distance, and shoulder proprioception in patients with subacromial impingement syndrome.

A total of 72 patients aged 18-65 years diagnosed with subacromial impingement syndrome will be randomly assigned to three groups: (1) conventional shoulder kinesio taping combined with therapeutic exercise, (2) scapular kinesio taping combined with therapeutic exercise, and (3) therapeutic exercise alone (control group).

All participants will receive the same supervised therapeutic exercise program three times per week for eight weeks, totaling 24 sessions. Participants in the two kinesio taping groups will additionally receive their respective taping interventions three times per week for eight weeks.

Outcome assessments will be performed at baseline and after eight weeks of treatment by an assessor blinded to group allocation.

The primary outcome will be acromiohumeral distance measured by ultrasonography at 0° and 60° of shoulder abduction. Secondary outcomes will include pain intensity assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), shoulder pain and disability assessed using the Shoulder Pain and Disability Index (SPADI), health-related quality of life assessed using the Western Ontario Rotator Cuff Index (WORC), and shoulder proprioception assessed using an active joint repositioning test.

The study aims to determine whether adding kinesio taping to therapeutic exercise provides additional benefits and whether the effects differ between conventional shoulder and scapular taping techniques.
primary_outcomes: Change in Acromiohumeral Distance (AHD) Measured by Ultrasonography
title: Effects of Different Kinesio Taping Methods in Subacromial Impingement Syndrome

brief_summary:
The purpose of this randomized controlled trial is to evaluate whether a school-based Trauma-Informed Psychosocial Competence (TIPC) intervention can reduce nonsuicidal self-injury among adolescents in China. Nonsuicidal self-injury means deliberately injuring oneself without intending to die.

The TIPC program aims to help adolescents understand and accept themselves, manage difficult emotions, cope with stress, communicate with others, and seek support. It uses a trauma-informed approach that recognizes how stressful or adverse experiences may affect young people and emphasizes safety, respect, and supportive relationships.

The main question is whether adolescents receiving the TIPC program show a greater reduction in nonsuicidal self-injury than those in the comparison group. The study will also examine changes in emotional well-being and psychosocial functioning.

Participants will be assigned to an intervention group or a comparison group through random allocation. Adolescents in the intervention group will take part in structured school-based sessions. Participants in both groups will complete questionnaires before and after the intervention to assess self-injury and related psychological and social outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Past-Month Nonsuicidal Self-Injury Behavior Frequency Score
Change From Baseline in Past-Month Nonsuicidal Self-Injury Thought Frequency Score
title: Effects of a School-Based Trauma-Informed Psychosocial Competence Intervention on Nonsuicidal Self-Injury in Adolescents

brief_summary:
This research trial will test whether using carbon dioxide as a contrast medium during surgery to open blocked leg arteries can prevent kidney injury. One in five people over 55 in the UK suffer with narrowing or blockages in their leg arteries, which is called peripheral arterial disease. It leads to poor leg circulation, which can cause leg gangrene or infection. Sometimes this may even lead to major lower limb amputation. To prevent this from happening, the affected arteries can be opened using endovascular revascularisation. These procedures are the most common artery surgeries in the NHS. To be able to perform these procedures, doctors use an iodine-based contrast medium (dye) injected in the artery, which can negatively affect kidney function.

Instead of the usual dye that causes kidney problems, carbon dioxide can be used as it does not damage the kidneys. No previous randomised controlled trial, however, has tested whether using carbon dioxide via automated injectors does indeed protect the kidneys in these procedures.

This research will take place in at least six NHS hospitals in the UK. People with peripheral arterial disease and chronic kidney disease who are having a procedure to open their arteries will be asked to take part. Participants will be randomly chosen to have the procedure with carbon dioxide or with standard iodine-based contrast medium. The investigators will then perform blood tests to measure serum creatinine on the 2nd, 30th, and 90th day after the procedure to compare kidney function between the two groups. The investigators will also compare the volume of iodine-based contrast medium used. The study will also include qualitative research into how the hospital staff performing the intervention feel, as well as how participants found the procedure with carbon dioxide.
primary_outcomes: Renal Function: Log Serum Creatinine
title: Preventing Kidney Injury Using Carbon Dioxide as Contrast Medium in Patients With Peripheral Arterial Disease (PAD) and Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) Having Arterial Intervention

brief_summary:
Older adults with hip fracture often experience severe pain before and after surgery. This pain can cause anxiety and poor sleep, and may increase the risk of postoperative delirium (sudden confusion after surgery). A fascia iliaca compartment block (FICB) is an injection of numbing medicine near the hip nerves that relieves pain, but standard numbing medicines only last about 8 to 12 hours. Liposomal bupivacaine is a long-acting form of a numbing medicine that may relieve pain for up to 72 hours after a single injection.

This study tests whether giving an ultrasound-guided FICB with liposomal bupivacaine immediately after hospital admission (before surgery) improves sleep quality, reduces anxiety and pain, lowers the need for opioid pain medicines, and reduces postoperative delirium in patients aged 65 to 80 years undergoing surgery for intertrochanteric hip fracture, compared with a placebo (saline) injection. All participants in both groups receive the same standard pain treatment, including scheduled intravenous dexketoprofen and patient-controlled analgesia after surgery.
primary_outcomes: Leeds Sleep Evaluation Questionnaire (LSEQ) score on the night of admission
title: Liposomal Bupivacaine Fascia Iliaca Block for Perioperative Sleep Quality in Elderly Patients With Intertrochanteric Fracture

brief_summary:
This study evaluated the effects of generative artificial intelligence (GAI)-assisted education on clinical reasoning performance among traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) interns.

An assessor-blinded, nonrandomized, cluster-controlled educational intervention study was conducted at three hospital branches in Taiwan. Participants were assigned to either a GAI-assisted education group or a conventional education group according to their clinical training sites.

The intervention group received a three-hour introductory training session on ChatGPT and was encouraged to use the tool independently for clinical case analysis during subsequent clinical rotations. The control group received conventional clinical education without structured GAI-assisted training.

The primary outcome was clinical reasoning performance, assessed through clinical case reports independently evaluated by two blinded TCM educators. Secondary outcomes included perceptions of the four-element TCM diagnostic framework and perceptions of GAI-assisted learning.
primary_outcomes: Change in Clinical Reasoning Performance Score
title: Generative AI-Assisted Teaching and Clinical Reasoning Among TCM Interns

brief_summary: The PREVENT-R trial will evaluate an intervention targeting both clinician and patient behavior. The clinician-focused piece consists of an electronic medical record-based digital nudge presented to emergency department clinicians caring for eligible older adults at high risk of readmission. The nudge is intended to prompt clinicians to consider referral to the Service Navigator Program from the Agency on Aging of South Central Connecticut for patients with needs that may be addressed through community-based services and supports. The study will evaluate whether these mechanisms (clinician referral and patient program acceptance behavior) are associated with subsequent Emergency Department (ED) revisits and 30-day hospital re-admissions.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of participants with hospital readmissions
title: A Clinician-Patient Dual Behavior Change Framework to Leverage Informed Digital Nudges to Reduce Hospital Readmissions and Improve Patient Outcomes: A Trial for Scalable Strategy to Reduce Readmissions (PREVENT-R)

brief_summary:
The PRISM-CM study will test whether 810-nanometer laser acupuncture reduces migraine days and related symptoms in adults with chronic migraine. Laser acupuncture uses low-level laser light at acupuncture points without inserting needles. The study will also assess safety and explore whether clinical features, traditional Chinese medicine syndrome patterns, and brain function are associated with differences in treatment response.

This study will enroll 135 participants at Taichung Veterans General Hospital: 90 patients with chronic migraine and 45 healthy volunteers. After keeping a headache diary for 4 weeks before treatment, patients will be assigned by chance to active laser acupuncture or sham laser acupuncture, with 45 patients in each group. Sham treatment uses the same acupuncture points and procedures but does not deliver therapeutic laser energy. Healthy volunteers will not be randomized and will receive active laser acupuncture as a comparison group. All three groups will receive 8 sessions over 4 weeks.

Patients with chronic migraine, outcome assessors, and staff analyzing brain images and study data will not be told which treatment was assigned. The practitioners providing treatment will know the assignment.

All participants will complete questionnaires and standardized traditional Chinese medicine assessments before treatment and monthly through 12 months after treatment begins. The traditional Chinese medicine assessments use symptom questions, tongue images, and pulse examinations to identify patterns of signs and symptoms, called syndrome patterns. Patients with chronic migraine will also continue recording headache diaries. The main outcome is the change in the number of migraine days per month from before treatment to week 12. Other outcomes include headache severity and duration, days using medicines to treat headache attacks, headache-related limitations, anxiety and depressive symptoms, sleep, sensitivity to light and sound, quality of life, and adverse events.

All three groups will undergo brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) before treatment and at week 12 after treatment begins. An additional MRI at week 4 is optional and depends on participant willingness and study resources. The scans will examine brain structure, connections between brain regions, and brain activity at rest and during laser stimulation of acupuncture points.

Researchers will compare active and sham treatment in patients with chronic migraine. Healthy volunteers will provide a reference for brain imaging and questionnaire findings but will not be included in the main analysis of migraine treatment effects. Exploratory analyses will examine whether clinical features and traditional Chinese medicine syndrome patterns before treatment are associated with greater or smaller treatment benefits. brief_summary: The present study aims to design, develop and test an electronic archive to be able to track over time the so-called Patient-Specific Cutting Guides for Orthopedics (in English often known as ' Pa-tient-Specific Cutting Guides'). From a technical standpoint, it will be necessary to evaluate whether the compilation of the con-trolled-access archive of these surgical guides will be provided and automated by the software tools currently used for their design, or whether the use of an additional standard platform (such as REDCap) will be deemed suitable, or whether the development of an ad-hoc database will be necessary.

This study investigated the effects of sports massage and modified traditional Thai massage on delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS) and recovery following strenuous exercise in healthy, physically inactive young men.

The study used a randomized, three-condition, three-period crossover design. Participants completed an exercise protocol designed to induce muscle soreness and subsequently received one of three recovery interventions: sports massage, modified traditional Thai massage, or passive recovery. Each participant underwent all three conditions in a randomized sequence, with a washout period between experimental sessions.

The recovery interventions were administered approximately six hours after exercise. Muscle soreness, pressure pain threshold, flexibility, vertical jump performance, and perceived physical performance were assessed at baseline and at 24 and 48 hours after exercise.

The study aimed to compare the effects of the two massage approaches with passive recovery on perceived muscle soreness, mechanical pain sensitivity, and functional recovery following exercise-induced muscle damage.

This prospective observational study included 146 patients aged 18-70 years with American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status I-II. Preoperative sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Postoperative pain was evaluated using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), including assessments during the early postoperative period and at the three-month follow-up.

The study aimed to determine whether poor sleep quality before surgery was associated with greater postoperative pain. No additional medical interventions were performed as part of the research, and all patients received routine clinical care.

This prospective randomized clinical study evaluates a novel physiology-oriented mild ovarian stimulation protocol based on the delayed initiation of corifollitropin alfa. Unlike conventional ovarian stimulation, which begins during the early follicular phase, the proposed protocol postpones exogenous gonadotropin administration until cycle day 4, allowing physiological follicular recruitment to occur before ovarian stimulation.

Participants are randomly assigned to one of two strategies for prevention of premature luteinizing hormone (LH) surge:

daily GnRH antagonist administration, or progesterone-primed ovarian stimulation (PPOS). The primary objective is to evaluate ovarian response and the feasibility of this simplified stimulation strategy. Secondary objectives include embryological outcomes, pregnancy outcomes, gonadotropin consumption, treatment burden, and the proportion of patients completing stimulation without supplementary gonadotropin administration.

The study aims to determine whether a physiology-oriented late-start stimulation protocol can simplify IVF treatment while maintaining satisfactory embryological and clinical outcomes.

brief_summary:
The goal of this study, conducted entirely using computer simulations, is to evaluate the projected long-term cardiovascular impact of the new ArmoLIPID Cholesterol Plus formulation in adults with mild-to-moderate hypercholesterolemia and low-to-moderate cardiovascular risk.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Does the addition of ArmoLIPID Cholesterol Plus to lifestyle management reduce the projected incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and non-fatal stroke?
* How does sustained LDL cholesterol reduction influence cumulative cardiovascular risk over 5, 10, 15, and 20 years?
* Could the use of ArmoLIPID Cholesterol Plus delay the projected need for statin therapy?

Researchers will compare two simulated strategies: lifestyle management alone versus lifestyle management combined with one daily tablet of the new ArmoLIPID Cholesterol Plus formulation.

No human participants will be recruited, treated, or followed in this study. Using the Aeterna Deep computational platform, researchers will generate a synthetic population of 100,000 digital twins whose characteristics reflect those of adults with mild-to-moderate hypercholesterolemia. The simulations will incorporate clinical evidence from previous studies and model individual cardiovascular trajectories over a 20-year period.

All cardiovascular outcomes will be computational projections rather than events observed in human participants.
primary_outcomes: Projected Cumulative Incidence of First Major Adverse Cardiovascular Event (MACE)
title: Long-Term Cardiovascular Impact of ArmoLIPID Cholesterol Plus: An In Silico Study Using Digital Twins

Thirteen healthy female volleyball players aged 10 to 14 years completed eight sessions. Each player performed a standardized 10-minute warm-up under four conditions: no music, music labelled 60 to 80 beats per minute, music labelled 90 to 110 beats per minute, and music labelled 120 to 140 beats per minute. The primary outcome was countermovement jump height. Secondary outcomes were jump-derived peak power, relative peak power, single-hand handgrip strength and rating of perceived exertion. Chronotype, subjective wellness, sleep quality and mood were assessed at baseline.

brief_summary:
Degenerative lumbar disease can cause back pain, leg pain, and difficulty with daily activities. Some patients require lumbar fusion surgery. In patients with low bone mass, the bones may provide less support for the interbody cage, an implant placed between two vertebrae. The cage may sink into the surrounding bone after surgery, a complication known as cage subsidence. Stress endplate augmentation strengthens the bone near the surfaces supporting the cage, but its benefits and risks require further evaluation.

This single-center prospective observational cohort study will compare outcomes in patients undergoing oblique lumbar interbody fusion (OLIF) with or without stress endplate augmentation. Consecutive eligible patients aged 50 years or older with low bone mass and degenerative lumbar disease will be enrolled before surgery and followed for 18 months afterward.

Whether stress endplate augmentation is performed will be determined by the treating surgeon and patient through routine clinical decision-making. The study will not assign treatment. Patients will be grouped according to whether they receive stress endplate augmentation.

The main outcome will be cage subsidence at 18 months after surgery. Other outcomes will include spinal fusion, changes in spinal measurements on imaging, back and leg pain, functional disability, surgical and hospitalization measures, and complications.

Clinical information, bone density measurements, imaging findings, and patient-reported outcomes will be collected before surgery and during follow-up. Comparisons will account for differences in patient characteristics and surgical factors. The study aims to clarify the benefits and risks associated with stress endplate augmentation in patients with low bone mass undergoing OLIF.
primary_outcomes: Cage Subsidence at 18 Months After Surgery
title: Comparing Lumbar Fusion With and Without Stress Endplate Augmentation in Patients With Low Bone Mass
