brief_summary:
Background: The leading cause of death worldwide is cardiovascular disease, with an estimated 19.8 million deaths per year. Coronary artery disease is a type of cardiovascular disease that can be treated with revascularisation interventions like coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and hybrid revascularisation (CABG and PCI). The COronary Revascularisation (CORE) Platform Trial is a multicentre, investigator-initiated, platform trial designed to evaluate several procedural and medical interventions for treatment of patients with coronary artery disease referred for coronary artery revascularisation.

Methods: This Master Protocol describes the overarching design, organisation, and methodology of the CORE Platform Trial. The target population will be adults with coronary artery disease referred for coronary artery revascularisation. The platform will allow interventions to be assessed in parallel or sequentially across separate domains, each with predefined sample sizes, outcomes, and statistical analysis plans. The CORE Platform Trial is guided by three overarching principles: to promote and establish international collaboration; to conduct pragmatic trials that generate findings applicable to routine clinical practice while avoiding compromise to methodological rigor; and to avoid unnecessary complexity in methodology and statistical analyses. The HYCORE1 trial serves as the initial domain within the platform, with future domains including colchicine; sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor; and hybrid versus PCI revascularisation. Randomisation will be web-based with allocation concealment, stratification by site and domain, and blinding where feasible.

Discussion: The CORE Platform Trial provides a collaborative, pragmatic, and methodologically rigorous framework for evaluating interventions in patients with coronary artery disease referred for coronary artery revascularisation. By using shared infrastructure and predefined domain-specific protocols, the platform aims to improve efficiency, reduce research waste, and strengthen the evidence base for coronary artery disease care.
lead_sponsor: Copenhagen Trial Unit, Center for Clinical Intervention Research
primary_outcomes: A composite outcome of either all-cause mortality, a diagnosis of spontaneous myocardial infarction, a diagnosis of stroke, or any unplanned hospitalization (the primary outcomes defined for the first randomised comparison in the CORE Platform Trial)
title: The CORE Platform Trial

brief_summary:
This study is a randomized controlled clinical trial focusing on the prevention of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), planned to start in May 2026 and end in April 2027. It primarily compares the efficacy and safety of amisulpride injection combined with ondansetron versus ondansetron alone in patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery. A centralized stratified block randomization method will be used. In the combination group, patients will receive a single intravenous injection of amisulpride 5 mg plus ondansetron 4 mg within 1-2 minutes after anesthesia induction, while the control group will receive ondansetron 4 mg alone. The study adopts a single-blind design, meaning that patients will not know their group assignment.

The primary objective is to evaluate the efficacy of the combination regimen in preventing PONV under different anesthesia methods. The primary endpoint is complete response (CR), defined as no vomiting or retching and no use of rescue antiemetic medication within 24 hours after surgery. Secondary endpoints include the incidence of nausea at 2, 6, 12, and 24 hours postoperatively, the proportion of patients with significant nausea (VAS \>4), the incidence of vomiting, and the proportion requiring rescue medication. The study will also assess safety, as well as the effects of the combination regimen on emergence agitation, postoperative delirium, shivering, recovery of bowel function, changes in inflammatory factors, postoperative pain, and analgesic consumption.

The study population consists of patients undergoing elective laparoscopic surgery under general anesthesia. After providing informed consent, eligible participants will undergo baseline assessment, including demographic information, medical history, PONV risk factors, comorbidities, medication history, vital signs, electrocardiogram, and laboratory tests. Postoperatively, blinded assessors will collect PONV-related information during the periods of 0-2 hours, 2-6 hours, and 6-24 hours, and will also record vital signs, adverse events, and concomitant medications. The primary efficacy endpoint will be assessed within 24 hours after surgery, while safety follow-up will usually continue until postoperative day 7 or discharge.

Sample size was calculated based on the primary endpoint of CR. According to previous studies, the expected CR rate is about 57% in the combination group and 46% in the ondansetron-alone group. Using a two-independent-sample proportion difference test with a two-sided alpha of 0.05 and beta of 0.20, 323 participants are required per group. Allowing for a 10% dropout rate, 359 participants will be enrolled in each group, for a total of 718 participants.

In terms of study management, the protocol clearly defines criteria for study completion, dropout, and early withdrawal. The study will be considered complete when the last participant has finished the day-7 telephone follow-up or early withdrawal visit, and all data cleaning, review, and statistical analyses have been completed. Reasons for withdrawal include withdrawal of informed consent, loss to follow-up, death, study termination by the investigator, as well as early discontinuation due to adverse events, intolerable toxicity, or major protocol deviations.

Data management emphasizes authenticity, completeness, and traceability. Demographic data, vital signs, laboratory tests, and ECG findings may be directly entered into the case report form (CRF). Data such as nausea scores, shivering grades, agitation/delirium assessments, pain scores, bowel function recovery, and drug administration records must first be documented in source records before being transcribed into the CRF. Statistical analyses will be performed using SAS version 9.4 or above. Both an efficacy analysis set and a safety analysis set will be defined. Analyses will be stratified by anesthesia method, with methods including stratified chi-square tests, repeated-measures analysis of variance, and t-tests, while also exploring the independent effects after adjustment for confounding factors such as age, sex, duration of surgery, and anesthesia method.

Overall, the study is relatively well designed, with clear randomization procedures, a well-defined primary endpoint, a reasonable sample size calculation, and a fairly complete plan for safety evaluation, statistical analysis, and data management. It is expected to provide clinically valuable evidence on the use of amisulpride combined with ondansetron for the prevention of PONV.
primary_outcomes: The primary endpoint is complete response (CR), defined as the absence of any vomiting or retching and no use of rescue antiemetic medication within 24 hours postoperatively.
title: Amisulpride Injection for the Prevention of Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting in Patients Undergoing Laparoscopic Surgery

brief_summary: This study was designed to evaluate the effects of breathing meditation, accompanied by virtual reality (VR)-enhanced nature videos, on anxiety, comfort, pain, and physiological parameters in patients undergoing angiography. brief_summary:
Newborn babies who have difficulty breathing may need breathing support to help them receive enough oxygen. Two commonly used methods are heated, humidified high-flow nasal cannula (HHFNC), which delivers warmed, moist air and oxygen through small tubes in the nose, and nasal continuous positive airway pressure (nCPAP), which helps keep the lungs open by delivering air and oxygen under gentle pressure through a nasal mask or tubes.

This study will compare these two methods in newborn babies born at 28 weeks of pregnancy or later who develop breathing difficulties within the first 24 hours after birth. The study will be conducted in the neonatal intensive care unit at PAF Hospital Islamabad and will include 100 newborn babies. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either HHFNC or nCPAP as their initial breathing support.

The main purpose is to compare how often each method fails to provide adequate breathing support within the first 72 hours, requiring a change to another form of breathing support or insertion of a breathing tube for mechanical ventilation. The study will also assess other outcomes, including nasal injury, survival until hospital discharge, need for surfactant treatment, duration of breathing support and oxygen therapy, time to achieve full feeding, intestinal complications, and length of hospital stay.

The findings may help improve understanding of the effectiveness and safety of these two breathing support methods in newborn babies with breathing difficulties.

Implant planning and surgical guide fabrication will be performed using standardized digital workflows under the supervision of an experienced implant planning specialist. Postoperative CBCT imaging will be used to evaluate deviations between the planned and actual implant positions. The study will assess the accuracy of both planning approaches to determine whether AI-assisted planning provides comparable or improved implant placement accuracy relative to conventional planning.

Newborns will be assigned to either a leg and foot massage group or a control group. Pain will be assessed during the heel stick procedure using a neonatal pain assessment tool. The study will determine whether leg and foot massage can reduce pain associated with heel stick in newborns.

brief_summary:
Sleep disturbances are common among older adults residing in long-term care facilities. Warm-water footbaths may help improve sleep quality; however, different immersion depths may affect the body's response to warming.

This study examined the effects of warm-water footbaths at different immersion depths on subjective and objective sleep quality among older adults living in long-term care facilities.

A total of 40 older adults aged 65 years or older from six long-term care facilities in southern Taiwan participated in a crossover study. The study compared three conditions: ankle-level footbaths, below-knee footbaths, and routine care without a footbath.

During the footbath interventions, participants immersed both feet in water at 42°C for 15 minutes approximately one hour before bedtime. Subjective sleep quality was assessed using the Verran and Snyder-Halpern Sleep Scale, and objective sleep quality was measured using wrist actigraphy.
primary_outcomes: Subjective Sleep Quality Measured by the Verran and Snyder-Halpern Sleep Scale

title: Effects of Different Footbath Immersion Depths on Sleep Quality Among Older Adults in Long-Term Care Facilities

brief_summary: This phase II studies how well natalizumab works in preventing immune effector cell associated neurologic syndrome (ICANS) in patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) or mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) that has come back after a period of improvement (recurrent) or that does not respond to treatment (refractory) receiving chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy. A major complication of CAR T-cell therapy is ICANS. ICANS is inflammation of the brain or nerves. ICANS currently requires high-dose corticosteroid treatment which can inhibit CAR T-cell response. Natalizumab prevents immune cells from traveling from the blood to the fluid around the brain, which is a process thought to play a major role in CAR T-cell related brain injury. Natalizumab may be safe and effective in decreasing the frequency of severe ICANS in patients with DLBCL or MCL receiving CAR T-cell therapy.
lead_sponsor: University of Michigan Rogel Cancer Center

title: Natalizumab for the Prevention of ICANS in Patients With Recurrent or Refractory Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma or Mantle Cell Lymphoma Receiving CAR T-Cell Therapy

brief_summary:
Background Melasma is a chronic acquired pigmentary disorder characterized by symmetrical hyperpigmented macules and patches, predominantly affecting the face. It commonly occurs in individuals with darker skin phototypes and may significantly affect quality of life. Triple-combination cream containing hydroquinone, tretinoin, and fluocinolone acetonide is an established treatment; however, response may be incomplete. Microneedling enhances transdermal drug delivery and promotes dermal remodeling. Tranexamic acid (TXA) inhibits melanogenesis, while platelet-rich plasma (PRP) contains growth factors that may promote dermal remodeling and modulate melanogenesis.

Objective To compare the efficacy and safety of triple-combination cream plus microneedling with TXA versus platelet-rich plasma in the treatment of moderate-to-severe melasma.

Methods This randomized controlled trial will be conducted in the Department of Dermatology and Venereology, Bangladesh Medical University, over 12 months from protocol acceptance. Patients aged 18-60 years with symmetric facial melasma fulfilling the eligibility criteria will be randomly allocated into two equal groups. Group A will receive triple-combination cream containing fluocinolone acetonide 0.01%, hydroquinone 4%, and tretinoin 0.05% on alternate nights for 12 weeks, along with monthly microneedling with TXA for three sessions. Group B will receive the same cream regimen along with monthly microneedling with PRP for three sessions. Efficacy will be assessed using the modified Melasma Area and Severity Index (mMASI) score. Patient satisfaction and adverse events will also be assessed during follow-up. Appropriate statistical methods will be used for comparison between the groups. Ethical approval will be obtained from the Institutional Review Board of Bangladesh Medical University.

Results Results will be assessed and presented after completion of the study. Conclusion Conclusion will be drawn after completion of the study. Keywords: Melasma, tranexamic acid, platelet-rich plasma, microneedling, triple-combination cream, mMASI.
interventions: Group B (Triple Combination Cream + Microneedling + Platelet-Rich Plasma)
primary_outcomes: Group A: Triple-combination cream + microneedling with tranexamic acid solution. Group B: Triple-combination cream + microneedling with platelet-rich plasma.
title: Efficacy and Safety of Triple-Combination Cream Plus Microneedling Along With Tranexamic Acid Versus Platelet-Rich Plasma in the Treatment of Moderate-to-Severe Melasma: A Randomized Comparative Study

brief_summary:
This study evaluates whether an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted gait report generated from smartphone walking videos can support remote follow-up after total knee arthroplasty (TKA).

Patients complete standardized walking video recordings and symptom assessments before surgery and at approximately 6 and 12 weeks after surgery. The system analyzes the videos and provides gait information, including walking speed, step characteristics, gait symmetry, gait phases, knee movement, and changes over time.

A separate clinician evaluation examines whether these AI-generated gait reports improve remote clinical decision-making. Clinicians review postoperative cases using either usual remote information, including patient-reported symptoms and the original walking video, or the same information supplemented with the AI-generated gait report. The study evaluates the clinical acceptability of management recommendations, agreement with in-person clinical assessments, clinician confidence, need for additional information, and decision time.

The study also evaluates the feasibility, usability, and trust associated with home-based smartphone gait assessment from both patient and clinician perspectives. The AI gait report is intended to support postoperative monitoring and communication and does not replace clinical diagnosis or scheduled in-person follow-up.
interventions: video recorded on a mobile phone (assessed by doctors)
lead_sponsor: Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine
primary_outcomes: Number and proportion of physician-case remote management recommendations classified as clinically acceptable compared with the in-person reference assessment
title: Smartphone Video-Based AI Gait Analysis Reports to Support Remote Follow-up After Total Knee Arthroplasty

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate whether a single local application of L-arginine - a naturally occurring amino acid - into the gum pocket, in addition to standard treatment, can improve healing outcomes in patients with gum disease (periodontitis). The study is being conducted at the Faculty of Dentistry of Alanya Alaaddin Keykubat University and has received ethical approval from the Antalya Provincial Health Directorate Ethics Committee.

Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease in which the tissues and bone supporting the teeth are gradually damaged by bacteria. If left untreated, it can lead to tooth loss. The current standard treatment involves deep cleaning of the tooth root surfaces to reduce the bacterial load. This study tests whether adding an L-arginine solution to this treatment provides additional benefit, as laboratory and animal studies have shown that L-arginine has anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and bone-regeneration-supporting effects.

Sixty volunteers aged 18-65, diagnosed with Stage III periodontitis and who have not received any periodontal treatment in the past six months, will be enrolled. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups: one group will receive L-arginine solution and the other will receive saline solution (placebo) applied into the gum pocket. Gum pocket depth, inflammatory markers, and bone levels will be assessed at baseline and at 3 months after treatment. The total follow-up period for each participant will be 3 months.

Participation is entirely voluntary; participants have the right to withdraw from the study at any time. No serious risks are anticipated, and all personal information will be kept strictly confidential.
primary_outcomes: Change in Probing Pocket Depth (PPD)
title: NON-SURGİCAL PERİODONTAL THERAPY WİTH L-ARGİNİNE

brief_summary: This is a Phase 2 trial to evaluate the efficacy, safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of oral epetraborole tablets for the treatment of adults with phlebotomy-dependent polycythemia vera (PV). The trial is designed to confirm the safety profile of oral epetraborole in the PV patient population and to identify 1 or more oral epetraborole doses for the treatment of phlebotomy-dependent PV. The study consists of an open-label Sentinel Cohort, an open-label Dose Selection Cohort (Part 1), followed by a double-blind, randomized, Placebo-Controlled Cohort (Part 2), and an optional Open-Label Extension (OLE) Cohort (Part 3)
primary_outcomes: Part 2: Proportion of Participants per Treatment Group Maintaining Clinical Success defined as hematocrit control, not undergoing therapeutic phlebotomy and completing 12 weeks of treatment in Part 2
title: Phase 2 Study of Oral Epetraborole in Adults With Polycythemia Vera

brief_summary:
Pneumonia is a major cause of critical illness and respiratory failure, particularly among patients requiring invasive mechanical ventilation. These patients frequently experience systemic inflammation and metabolic disturbances, which can be assessed using the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and blood lactate levels. Pulmonary-specific enteral nutrition, characterized by a lower carbohydrate and higher fat composition, may help improve respiratory metabolism and modulate inflammatory responses.

This double-blind, randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate the effects of pulmonary-specific enteral nutrition compared with standard enteral nutrition on NLR and blood lactate levels in adult patients with pneumonia requiring invasive mechanical ventilation. Participants were randomly assigned to receive either pulmonary-specific enteral nutrition or standard enteral nutrition. NLR and blood lactate levels were measured on days 1, 3, and 5 to assess changes in inflammatory and metabolic parameters during the intervention period.
primary_outcomes: Change in Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (NLR) From Baseline to Day 5
title: Pulmonary-Specific Enteral Nutrition in Mechanically Ventilated Patients With Pneumonia

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate whether adding a suprazygomatic maxillary nerve block to the standard palatal nerve block improves pain control after cleft palate repair surgery in children. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either the standard palatal block alone or the standard palatal block combined with a suprazygomatic maxillary nerve block. Both techniques use medications commonly used for pain management during surgery.

The purpose of this study is to determine whether the addition of the suprazygomatic maxillary nerve block reduces postoperative pain, decreases the need for opioid medications, and improves recovery after cleft palate repair. Researchers will compare pain scores, medication use, recovery outcomes, and any treatment-related complications between the two groups.

Information collected from this study may help identify the most effective regional anesthesia approach for children undergoing cleft palate repair and may improve postoperative pain management and patient recovery.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Pain Scores
title: Comparative Study of Regional Nerve Blocks in Primary Cleft Palate Repair

brief_summary:
This prospective, single-arm interventional study will investigate why adults receiving the same prescribed dose and relative intensity of exercise show divergent changes in energy balance, body weight, and body composition. A total of 150 sedentary Chinese adults aged 18-40 years with overweight or obesity will complete a 12-week, supervised treadmill exercise programme. Exercise will be performed five times per week at an intensity corresponding to 60% of each participant's measured maximal oxygen uptake. Prescribed exercise energy expenditure will increase progressively from 150 kcal per session in Weeks 1-4 to 250 kcal per session in Weeks 5-8 and 350 kcal per session in Weeks 9-12.

The primary objective is to quantify inter-individual variability in energy compensation after the standardized intervention. Detailed measurements will characterize total and resting energy expenditure, energy intake, appetite, physical activity, body composition, glucose dynamics, cardiorespiratory fitness, brain responses to food-related stimuli, and molecular phenotypes. Multi-omics analyses will include gut microbiome, metabolomic, proteomic, extracellular-vesicle, peripheral blood mononuclear cell, and transcriptomic assessments. The study will explore physiological, behavioral, and molecular factors associated with divergent compensatory responses. No randomized comparator group is included; therefore, causal comparisons between exercise and non-exercise conditions are outside the study scope.
lead_sponsor: Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology ,Chinese Academy of Sciences
primary_outcomes: Energy compensation after the 12-week supervised exercise intervention
title: Individual Variability in Energy Compensation After a 12-Week Supervised Exercise Intervention

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to find out if a new digital surgical guide helps dentists perform esthetic crown lengthening more accurately than the current digital guide in adults with a gummy smile caused by altered passive eruption. Esthetic crown lengthening is a procedure that reshapes the gums and the bone around the teeth to show more of the natural tooth. The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Does the new digital guide help dentists reshape the bone and gums more accurately? Does the new digital guide improve healing, the appearance of the gums, the time needed for surgery, and participants' satisfaction with the results?

Researchers will compare a new stackable digital guide with the current digital guide to see if the new design provides more accurate and predictable results.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to have surgery using either the new digital guide or the current digital guide.
* Have dental examinations, digital mouth scans, and three-dimensional dental X-rays before surgery to plan their treatment.
* Have esthetic crown lengthening surgery using the assigned guide.
* Return for follow-up visits right after surgery and again about 6 weeks and 6 months later so researchers can check healing and compare the planned treatment with the final result.
* Answer questions about their satisfaction with the treatment and any pain medicine they used after surgery.
conditions: Gummy Smile of Altered Passive Eruption Type 1B
primary_outcomes: Difference in accuracy of both guides
title: Accuracy of Stackable Double Periodontal Guide in Esthetic Crown Lengthening

brief_summary:
Degenerative scoliosis can cause back pain, leg pain, difficulty walking, and impaired daily functioning. When spinal fusion is required, choosing the appropriate fusion extent remains challenging. Short-segment fusion involves fewer spinal levels, whereas long-segment fusion offers greater potential for deformity correction but requires more extensive surgery. It remains uncertain which patients are more likely to benefit from each strategy.

This multicenter prospective observational cohort study will investigate whether preoperative spinal alignment modifies the comparative clinical benefit of short-segment and long-segment fusion. Patients will receive surgery selected through routine clinical decision-making, without treatment assignment by the study. Clinical information, standing spinal radiographs, and patient-reported outcomes will be collected before surgery and during postoperative follow-up.

The primary outcome will be clinically meaningful improvement in the Scoliosis Research Society-22r subtotal score at 24 months after surgery. The study aims to identify patient subgroups with greater benefit from either fusion strategy and to develop clinically interpretable criteria that may support individualized selection of fusion extent.
primary_outcomes: Achievement of the Minimum Clinically Important Difference in the Scoliosis Research Society-22r Subtotal Score
title: Scoliosis Treatment: Evaluating Patient Suitability

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to better understand why some adults with cystic fibrosis (CF) continue to have repeated pulmonary exacerbations, or episodes of worsening respiratory symptoms, despite treatment with highly effective CFTR modulator therapy. The study will focus on whether a type of inflammation called type 2 (T2) inflammation may contribute to these pulmonary exacerbations.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Are signs of T2 inflammation more common in adults with CF who have frequent pulmonary exacerbations?

Are there differences in inflammation in the nose and airways between people who have frequent pulmonary exacerbations and those who do not?

How do immune cells and inflammation change during a pulmonary exacerbation?

Participants will:

Allow researchers to collect information about their CF and pulmonary exacerbations from their medical records.

Complete questionnaires about respiratory and sinus symptoms and quality of life.

Provide research blood samples, samples from inside the nose, and exhaled breath condensate.

Be followed for up to approximately 3 years, with additional research samples collected during qualifying pulmonary exacerbations when feasible.

Participants will continue to receive their usual CF medical care. No experimental medications or treatments will be given as part of this study.
primary_outcomes: Baseline Stable-State Absolute Peripheral Blood Eosinophil Count
title: Type 2 Inflammation in Adults With Cystic Fibrosis

brief_summary:
People who have had a sarcoma removed from the leg often live with weak muscles, stiff joints, and trouble walking. These problems can last for years. Formal medical follow-up usually ends about five years after treatment. Few studies have tested exercise at this stage.

This study tested an 8-week supervised exercise program. Participants were adults aged 18 to 67 who were at least 5 years past limb-sparing (wide resection) surgery for a leg sarcoma. They attended a clinic in Perth, Western Australia, twice a week for one hour. The program built leg strength, joint movement, balance, walking, and fitness. It progressed through three phases and was matched to each person's surgery and ability.

All participants received the same program type. There was no comparison group. Each person was tested twice before starting to confirm stable function. Testing was repeated at the end of the 8 weeks. It was repeated again 8 weeks later, after a period with no supervised exercise.

The main outcome was high-level mobility, measured by the High-level Mobility Assessment Tool (HiMAT). This tool scores walking, running, hopping, and stair climbing. Other outcomes were six-minute walk distance, leg strength, joint range of motion, and self-reported physical function and quality of life (TESS and SF-36 questionnaires).

The study aimed to learn two things. First, whether exercise improves strength and mobility years after sarcoma surgery. Second, whether those gains last after supervision stops.
conditions: Sarcoma of Bone and Connective Tissue
primary_outcomes: High-level Mobility Assessment Tool, HiMAT
title: Exercise Rehabilitation to Improve Long-term Outcomes in Sarcoma Survivors.

brief_summary:
This study evaluates an adaptation of Specialist Supportive Clinical Management (SSCM) for children and adolescents aged 13-17 years with anorexia nervosa or atypical anorexia nervosa receiving outpatient treatment at the Stockholm Centre for Eating Disorders. SSCM may be offered when other recommended treatments, such as Family-Based Treatment (FBT) or Enhanced Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT-E), are not considered suitable.

The primary aim is to evaluate the feasibility and adherence of SSCM for children and adolescents, including treatment completion and attendance. The study will also explore preliminary treatment effects, including changes in eating disorder symptoms, weight, psychological symptoms, and functioning. Participants and their caregivers will complete assessments before, during, and after treatment, with a follow-up three months after treatment completion. Patients and caregivers will also be invited to participate in qualitative interviews at the end of treatment to explore their experiences of SSCM.
interventions: Specialist Supportive Clinical Management for Children and Adolescents (SSCM-Youth)
primary_outcomes: Treatment completion
Treatment adherence
Patients' and Parents' or Legal Guardians' Experiences of SSCM
title: Specialist Supportive Clinical Management (SSCM) for Children and Adolescents With Anorexia Nervosa and Atypical Anorexia Nervosa

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to investigate whether different amounts of plyometric exercise without jumping can improve lower-limb muscle strength, power, and muscle and tendon mechanical properties in sedentary and/or physically inactive older adults.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does performing a higher amount of plyometric exercise without jumping lead to greater improvements in functional muscle strength and power than performing a lower amount?

Do different amounts of exercise produce different changes in the mechanical properties of muscles and tendons?

Researchers will compare three groups: a high-volume exercise group, a low-volume exercise group, and a control group that will not receive the exercise intervention. This comparison will help determine how the amount of exercise influences physical function and muscle and tendon properties.

Participants will:

Be randomly assigned to one of the three groups.

Complete physical assessments before and after the eight-week study period, including tests of lower-limb strength, power, and muscle and tendon mechanical properties.

If assigned to an exercise group, participate in supervised plyometric exercise sessions without jumping twice a week for eight weeks.

If assigned to the control group, continue their usual daily activities without participating in the exercise program during the study.
primary_outcomes: Peak Functional Lower-Limb Force
Peak Functional Lower-Limb Power
title: Effects of Different Amounts of Plyometric Exercise Without Jumping in Physically Inactive Older Adults

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate the clinical efficacy of intraperitoneal hydrocortisone 100 mg administration in reducing postoperative pain and inflammatory response in patients undergoing elective Caesarean section under spinal anaesthesia combined with bilateral Transversus Abdominis Plane (TAP) block.

Postoperative pain following Caesarean section stems from both visceral and somatic surgical trauma. While TAP block effectively attenuates somatic wound pain, visceral pain mediated by peritoneal irritation remains a significant component of acute postoperative discomfort. Intraperitoneal instillation of local corticosteroids like hydrocortisone may modulate local inflammatory cascades, thereby reducing peritoneal nociceptor sensitization.

This double-blind randomized controlled trial involved 50 term pregnant women scheduled for elective Caesarean section under spinal anaesthesia with bilateral TAP block. Participants were randomly assigned to receive either 100 mg hydrocortisone in 100 mL NaCl 0.9% or 100 mL NaCl 0.9% placebo instilled into the peritoneal cavity prior to abdominal closure. Postoperative pain intensity (measured via Visual Analog Scale \[VAS\] at 6, 12, and 24 hours) and serum C-Reactive Protein (CRP) levels at 24 hours postoperatively were compared between the two groups.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Pain Intensity
title: Intraperitoneal Hydrocortisone for Postoperative Pain and CRP Following Caesarean Section

brief_summary: Pneumonia is the main cause of ICU admission in patients with acute respiratory failure (ARF). Severe pneumonia is a serious lung infection caused by bacteria, fungi, viruses, and other pathogens. It often leads to respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation. It is also accompanied by septic shock or multiple organ dysfunction, and patients need intensive care. The average mortality rate is 30%-40%. Therefore, there is an urgent need to find treatments that improve outcomes in patients with severe pneumonia. Inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) can selectively dilate pulmonary vessels in well-ventilated lung areas. This reduces pulmonary artery pressure, improves the ventilation/perfusion ratio, and increases oxygenation. At 80 ppm, iNO can effectively reduce mean pulmonary artery pressure and pulmonary vascular resistance. It also reduces oxidative stress and has anti-inflammatory effects. Short-term inhalation is safe. The level of positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) affects the effect of NO. Setting PEEP according to airway opening pressure (AOP) can deliver iNO efficiently to target areas. Based on this, we designed this randomized controlled trial to investigate whether a modified iNO regimen, PEEP set according to AOP combined with 80 ppm NO, improves outcomes in patients with acute respiratory failure receiving mechanical ventilation.
primary_outcomes: Ventilator-free days at day 28
title: Modified Inhaled Nitric Oxide in Ventilated Patients With Acute Respiratory Failure

brief_summary:
This study aimed to evaluate whether daily postbiotic supplementation could improve gastrointestinal well-being and influence physiological and metabolic parameters in healthy young adults.

A total of 22 healthy adults participated in this single-center, randomized, placebo-controlled pilot study. Participants were assigned to receive either a daily capsule containing 100 mg of a postbiotic preparation or a placebo for 12 weeks.

Gastrointestinal symptoms were assessed using the Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale (GSRS) before and after supplementation. Additional assessments included body composition, metabolic health, intestinal microbiota, inflammation, oxidative stress, and quality of life.

The study was designed to explore the potential beneficial effects of postbiotic supplementation on gastrointestinal health and related biological processes.
primary_outcomes: Change in Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale (GSRS) Score
title: The Impact of Postbiotic Supplementation on Tolerability and Physiological/Metabolic Parameters

brief_summary:
DrinkAge is a randomized controlled trial investigating whether increasing daily water intake can improve hydration and health-related outcomes in adults aged 60 years or older who habitually drink relatively little water.

The study will include 38 participants who habitually consume 35 mL/kg/day or less of water. Participants will be randomly assigned to either increase their daily water intake to at least 45 mL/kg/day or maintain their usual water intake for 7 days.

Before and after the 7-day intervention, participants will undergo assessments of hydration, blood and urine markers, hormone levels, body water distribution, body composition, muscle and physical function, mood, physical activity, and health-related quality of life.

The main purpose of the study is to determine whether increasing habitual water intake changes levels of arginine vasopressin, a hormone involved in the regulation of body water balance. The study will also investigate whether increasing water intake is associated with changes in hydration status, cardiovascular and kidney-related markers, stress-related hormones, body water distribution, physical performance, mood, and quality of life.

The results may help clarify whether increasing habitual water intake is a feasible strategy to improve hydration and support healthy ageing in older adults who habitually drink relatively little water.
primary_outcomes: Change in Serum Arginine Vasopressin Concentration
title: Effects of Increased Water Intake on Hormonal Response, Hydration Status, and Physical Function in Low-drinking Older Adults

brief_summary: This study will evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and preliminary efficacy of GBP-213 in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD).

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized, controlled simulation-based educational study is to compare the effectiveness of virtual reality (VR) and task trainer-based training in improving dysrhythmia management skills among intern physicians.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does VR-based training improve dysrhythmia management performance as effectively as task trainer-based training?
* Are the improvements in dysrhythmia management performance maintained four weeks after training?

Researchers will compare two groups of intern physicians receiving either VR-based training or task trainer-based training to evaluate differences in clinical performance and retention of acquired skills.

A total of 30 intern physicians will participate in the study, with 15 participants assigned to each group.

Participants will:

* Complete a baseline assessment using a high-fidelity patient simulator involving bradydysrhythmia, supraventricular tachycardia, and ventricular tachycardia scenarios.
* Receive practical dysrhythmia management training using either an immersive VR environment or a task trainer.
* Undergo an immediate post-training assessment using high-fidelity simulation scenarios.
* Complete a retention assessment four weeks after training to evaluate the maintenance of acquired skills.

Participant performance will be assessed using standardized checklists based on dysrhythmia management algorithms. Assessments will be video-recorded for subsequent evaluation.
primary_outcomes: Change in Dysrhythmia Management Performance Score From Baseline to Immediate Post-Training
title: Comparison of Task Trainer and Virtual Reality Approaches in Dysrhythmia Management Education

brief_summary: Post-operative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is a frequent complication of surgical aortic valve replacement, affecting 38 to 63% of patients, and increasing risks of stroke, heart failure, and long-term mortality. By intervening upstream of surgical stress, transcutaneous vagal nerve stimulation (tVNS) could act as an autonomic and anti-inflammatory preconditioning, stabilizing sympathovagal balance, reducing POAF susceptibility and post-operative outcomes. This pilot study evaluates the feasibility, tolerability, and biological activity of a preoperative tVNS protocol versus sham (1-2 hours/day), with ΔRMSSD, a non-invasive marker of parasympathetic modulation as the primary endpoint, inflammatory biomarkers, postoperative recovery, and cardiovascular events up to 3 months as secondary outcomes. This step is essential to identify a preoperative strategy that is practicable, well-tolerated, and capable of inducing measurable parasympathetic modulation prior to surgery and the prevention of POAF.
interventions: tVNS session on the left earlobe
tVNS "SHAM" session the conchae aurea of the left ear
lead_sponsor: Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Saint Etienne
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in RMSSD of Heart Rate Variability After the Last tVNS Session
title: Pilot Study to Determine the Optimal Protocol for Preoperative Transcutaneous Vagal Neurostimulation

brief_summary: This is a prospective, single-arm, single-center exploratory clinical study. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a triplet regimen-becotatug vedotin combined with anti-PD-1 and S-1-in patients with EGFR-positive advanced pancreatic cancer who have failed at least one line of standard systemic therapy. Pancreatic cancer is one of the most lethal malignancies, and patients who progress after first-line treatment have very limited effective options. The study plans to enroll 27 participants aged 18 years or older with histopathologically confirmed pancreatic cancer, evidence of recurrence or metastasis (or disease not amenable to complete surgical resection), EGFR positivity confirmed by immunohistochemistry, an ECOG performance status of 0 to 3, and at least one measurable target lesion. All participants will receive becotatug vedotin 2.0 mg/kg intravenously on Day 1 every three weeks, anti-PD-1 200 mg intravenously on Day 1 every three weeks, and oral S-1 40 to 60 mg twice daily on Days 1 to 14 followed by a 7-day rest, repeated every three weeks. Treatment will continue until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, completion of 12 months of treatment, or other protocol-defined discontinuation criteria. Tumor response will be assessed by CT or MRI every 9 weeks according to RECIST v1.1, and safety will be assessed according to NCI-CTCAE version 5.0. The primary endpoint is objective response rate (ORR). Secondary endpoints include disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DOR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. The study duration is approximately 3 years, with participant enrollment planned from OCT. 2026 to OCT. 2027. All participants will receive active treatment; no placebo is included. This study addresses a major unmet medical need, as current second-line and later treatment options for advanced pancreatic cancer provide only limited benefit.

brief_summary:
Endometrial cancer is one of the most common gynecological malignancies, and its incidence is rising. Currently, there is a lack of highly effective and non-invasive screening methods. Liquid biopsy, which analyzes cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in the blood, has emerged as a promising approach for early cancer detection. This observational study aims to develop and evaluate a non-invasive blood test to screen for early-stage endometrial cancer and to distinguish between benign and malignant endometrial lesions.

This study plans to enroll 512 female participants, divided into three groups: 216 patients with stage I-IV endometrial cancer, 80 patients with atypical endometrial hyperplasia (a precancerous condition), and 216 healthy controls. We will collect peripheral blood samples from all participants and perform low-pass whole-genome sequencing (WGS) on the extracted plasma cfDNA. By analyzing specific DNA features (such as DNA fragment patterns, end motifs, and copy number variations) and using artificial intelligence (machine learning), we will build a predictive model. This study hopes to establish a more effective, non-invasive early screening strategy to improve the clinical diagnosis of endometrial cancer in the Chinese population.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic performance (sensitivity and specificity) of the cfDNA fragmentomics model for early screening of endometrial cancer
title: Liquid Biopsy-Based Early Screening for Endometrial Cancer in Regional Chinese Populations

brief_summary:

Treatment regimen for eligible subjects:

Becotatug vedotin (MRG003): 2.0 mg/kg, administered intravenously on Day 1 of each 21-day cycle (Q3W), starting at least 30 minutes after completion of the ICI infusion.

Immune checkpoint inhibitor: Investigator's choice, including but not limited to camrelizumab, tislelizumab, and pembrolizumab; Q3W, IV, Day 1, with infusion duration per the respective prescribing information.

Multimodal radiotherapy: Initiated within the first 2 cycles of systemic therapy (no later than the end of Cycle 2), targeting the primary lesion and/or metastatic lesions. An individualized radiotherapy plan is delivered, using conventionally fractionated radiotherapy or stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT), at approximately 50-60 Gy in 25-30 fractions (or a biologically equivalent dose/fractionation schedule). Investigators may appropriately adjust the timing, dose, and fractionation. Whether the ICI is withheld during radiotherapy is left to the investigator's discretion based on the patient's clinical condition.

The goal of this observational study is to learn how well patients' own pain ratings match what an observer sees and whether the patient asks for extra pain medicine after total knee replacement surgery. The study will include adults aged 18 years or older having planned (elective) total knee replacement under spinal anesthesia.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the pain score reported by the patient (Numeric Rating Scale, 0-10) agree with the patient's request for additional pain medicine?
* Does the pain score reported by the patient agree with pain behavior rated by an observer (facial expression, body movements, and vocal expressions)?

No treatment will be changed for this study. All patients will receive the hospital's standard anesthesia and pain management.

Participants will:

* Rate their pain from 0 (no pain) to 10 (worst pain imaginable) at 2, 6, and 24 hours after surgery
* Be observed by a researcher who scores their pain behavior at the same time points

brief_summary:
Study Overview This study evaluates a proteogenomic screening platform to identify precise therapeutic targets for patients with advanced solid tumors. While traditional precision medicine relies on DNA sequencing (genomics), this research adds protein analysis (proteomics) to better understand how cancer cells function and respond to treatment.

1. Background and Purpose Standard genomic testing often fails to predict whether a patient will respond to a specific drug because DNA mutations do not always result in active protein expression. By integrating Whole Exome Sequencing (WES) with phosphoproteomics (the study of protein activation), this study aims to:

   * Identify active signaling networks that DNA testing alone might miss.
   * Evaluate the feasibility and cost-effectiveness of this integrated platform compared to traditional methods.
   * Help match patients to the most effective targeted therapies through a "Basket Trial" framework, where treatment is based on molecular signatures rather than where the cancer started in the body.
2. Target Population

   * Adults (19 years and older) with histologically confirmed metastatic or locally advanced solid tumors.
   * Patients with Stage III, IV, or those at a high risk of recurrence.
   * Participants must have a life expectancy of at least 3 months and a good performance status (ECOG 0-2).
3. Study Procedures

   * Specimen Collection: Researchers will collect tumor tissue through biopsy or surgery. To preserve the integrity of proteins, these samples must be snap-frozen (Fresh-Frozen) immediately after extraction.
   * Analysis: The study will analyze the tissue and blood samples to characterize the patient's unique proteogenomic profile.
   * Treatment Assignment: If a specific molecular variant is identified (such as HRD or ALK/ROS1/MET signatures), and a matching sub-protocol is available, the patient may be enrolled in a targeted therapy trial. Patients who do not meet these criteria will continue with the standard of care.
4. Expectations and Logistics This is a multicenter, prospective screening study involving a nationwide logistics system to ensure high-quality sample transport. The study aims to enroll a total of 2,800 subjects (approximately 560 per year) and is expected to continue through December 31, 2028.
5. Potential Benefits and Risks

   * Benefits: Participants may gain access to targeted therapies based on their cancer's specific molecular profile.
   * Risks: While the study does not add new invasive procedures beyond standard care, there are potential psychosocial risks related to genomic findings and the sharing of de-identified data for research purposes.
conditions: Targeted Therapy Based on HRD (Homologous Recombination Deficiency) and ALK/ROS1/MET Signatures
primary_outcomes: Rate of Successful Identification of Actionable Therapeutic Targets
title: Master Protocol for Basket Clinical Trials of Targeted Therapies Based on Proteome and Whole Exome Sequencing Screening in Patients With Advanced Solid Tumors

Assessments take place before training and at 12 weeks (the primary endpoint).

The study will address whether Tai Chi improves physical and mental health; reduces fatigue, anxiety, depression and pain; improves lower-limb strength, gait and balance; and improves quality of life and self-efficacy.

brief_summary:
This study tests whether a training program helps nurses better recognize and care for older adults with frailty in hospital emergency departments.

Frailty is a condition where older adults become more vulnerable to health problems. A small illness or injury can cause serious complications for a frail person. Emergency nurses often lack training to identify frailty quickly.

In this study, some nurses will take part in a structured training program. The program includes four modules covering what frailty is, how to screen for it, and what nurses can do to help. Other nurses will not receive the training during the study. All nurses will complete a survey before, right after, and three months after the training.

The study will take place in eight public hospital emergency departments in the Marrakech-Safi region of Morocco. A total of 144 nurses will take part.

Researchers will measure whether nurses in the training group have better knowledge, attitudes, and practices about frailty compared to those who did not receive training. Researchers will also check whether the improvements last after three months.

Hospitals are randomly assigned to either the training group or the comparison group. This is called a cluster randomized trial.

It also explored changes in anxiety, worry, mood, wellbeing, and depressive symptoms, and in how vivid and distressing the trained memories were.

brief_summary:
This study, titled "Evaluation of the effect of regular physical exercise in women with breast cancer on adjuvant hormone therapy," is a research project designed to see how guided exercise can help women recovering from breast cancer.

Here is a simple summary of the study:

Who is it for? The study includes 150 women who have finished their primary treatments (like surgery or chemotherapy) and are in the early stages of hormone therapy.

The Goal: Researchers want to understand how regular exercise improves quality of life, physical fitness, and nutrition. They are also studying how exercise affects the immune system and the gut microbiota (the healthy bacteria in your body).

The Exercise Program: Participants take part in a 16-week supervised program. It consists of two sessions per week: one in a gym and one in a swimming pool. These sessions are led by experts and are specifically adapted to each patient's physical condition and needs.

Using Technology: To help with the study, participants use a mobile app (IALIBIRD) and a wearable activity tracker (like a bracelet). These tools monitor daily steps, sleep quality, and heart rate, and allow patients to report how they feel.

Medical Check-ups: Throughout the study, patients have regular visits to the hospital for blood tests and to provide saliva and stool samples for biological analysis. They also have body scans (DXA) to measure bone health, muscle mass, and body fat.

Why is this important? While hormone therapy is a vital treatment, it can last for 5 to 10 years and cause side effects like extreme tiredness, joint pain, and anxiety. This study aims to prove that regular exercise is a safe and effective way to reduce these symptoms and help women feel better during their recovery.

brief_summary:
Pneumonia is a lung infection that can cause serious complications, especially when accompanied by sepsis. Sepsis can trigger excessive inflammation and abnormal blood clotting, potentially leading to organ damage and delayed recovery. Two blood markers, D-dimer and interleukin-6 (IL-6), may increase in patients with these conditions.

Lumbrokinase DLBS1033 (Disolf®) is an oral treatment derived from the earthworm Lumbricus rubellus. It has properties that may help break down fibrin, a protein involved in blood clot formation, and reduce inflammation.

This study aimed to determine whether adding Lumbrokinase DLBS1033 to standard hospital treatment could improve D-dimer and IL-6 levels, shorten the time needed to achieve clinical stability, and reduce the length of hospital stay in patients with pneumonia, sepsis, and hypercoagulability.

The study was conducted at Dr. Moewardi General Hospital in Surakarta, Indonesia. A total of 50 hospitalized patients were randomly assigned to two groups of 25 participants each. One group received standard treatment plus oral Lumbrokinase DLBS1033, while the other group received standard treatment plus a placebo containing no active study medicine. Neither the participants nor the blinded study investigators knew which treatment was assigned.

Blood samples were collected at three assessment points: baseline (H0), day 10 (H10), and a clinical stability-related assessment designated H+1. D-dimer and IL-6 levels were measured to assess changes in blood clotting activity and inflammation. Participants were also monitored for clinical stability using Halm's Criteria, length of hospital stay, and potential adverse events.

The study hypothesis was that Lumbrokinase DLBS1033, when added to standard treatment, would improve D-dimer and IL-6 levels and promote faster clinical recovery compared with standard treatment plus placebo.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in D-Dimer Level
Change From Baseline in Interleukin-6 (IL-6) Level
title: Effects of Lumbrokinase DLBS1033 on D-Dimer, Interleukin-6, and Clinical Outcomes in Patients With Pneumonia and Sepsis

brief_summary: This two-arm randomized controlled trial compared Sensory-Assisted Neuromuscular Exercise (Group A) with Electrical Stimulation (Group B) in 40 adults aged 40-65 with Kellgren-Lawrence Grade II-III knee osteoarthritis, recruited from Ziauddin Hospital and Nemat Begum Hamdard Hospital. Both interventions were given three times a week for eight weeks, with outcomes assessed at baseline, week 8, and week 12 across eighteen variables covering pain, stiffness, function, range of motion, muscle activation, strength, alignment, and quality of life. Both groups improved significantly, but the neuromuscular exercise group outperformed electrical stimulation on most outcomes by week 12. Only the HKA alignment angle remained unchanged in both groups, as expected for a fixed skeletal measure. The authors conclude that neuromuscular exercise should be prioritized as a first-line conservative treatment, with electrical stimulation serving as an adjunct.

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to understand whether a wearable sensor (the Nutromics Sensor Device) can accurately measure drug and biomarker levels in the fluid just under the skin (interstitial fluid), instead of needing repeated blood draws, in adults admitted to hospital who are being treated with the antibiotic vancomycin or who are being monitored for signs of sepsis. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How closely do interstitial fluid levels of vancomycin match levels measured in the blood at the same time?
* How closely do interstitial fluid levels of creatinine, C-reactive protein, and lactate (biomarkers linked to kidney function, inflammation, and infection severity) match levels measured in the blood?
* Can the device pick up on early biomarker trends that signal a patient may be developing acute kidney injury?
* How well does the device work overall, and does it perform consistently across different patients (by age, sex, ethnicity, body size, and health conditions) and over time?
* Is the device safe to wear?

There is no comparison group receiving a different treatment. This study looks at how well the device's readings line up with standard blood tests, not about testing a new treatment.

Participants will:

* Wear up to two small sensor patches on their upper arm during their hospital stay (up to 5 days), with each patch replaced every 48 hours
* Have blood samples taken as part of their routine care so results can be compared
* Have their medical records reviewed 30 days after finishing the study to check on their health outcomes

brief_summary:
This prospective observational study will describe the anatomical relationship between two major blood vessels on the right side of the neck: the internal jugular vein and the common carotid artery. These vessels lie close together, and their relative positions are relevant when placing a central venous catheter.

The study will enroll 200 adults undergoing elective cardiac surgery at Ankara Bilkent City Hospital who require right internal jugular vein catheterization as part of their routine care. A single ultrasound image will be recorded for each participant under standardized conditions after general anesthesia and before catheter placement.

Computer-assisted image analysis will determine the angular position of the artery around the center of the vein on a 0°-360° scale. The study will describe the distribution of these angles and their frequencies within eight anatomical sectors. The findings may provide a more detailed quantitative description of neck vascular anatomy and support future research on ultrasound-guided central venous access. Participation will not alter routine anesthesia or catheterization management.
interventions: Standardized Ultrasound Imaging and Computer-Assisted Angular Mapping
primary_outcomes: Angular Position of the Right Common Carotid Artery Center Relative to the Right Internal Jugular Vein Center
title: Ultrasound Mapping of the Anatomical Relationship Between the Right Internal Jugular Vein and Carotid Artery

This study aims to investigate the effect of high-intensity aerobic exercise on pain threshold and blood pressure in females with primary dysmenorrhea. brief_summary:
The purpose of the project is to compare the efficacy of parasacral transcutaneous electric nerve stimulation (TENS) versus standard second-line therapy (oral anticholinergics) for pediatric patients with overactive bladder (OAB) and lower urinary tract dysfunction who have previously failed standard urotherapy. The investigators aim to evaluate the changes in lower urinary tract symptoms, quality of life scores, adherence to treatment, and parental/patient satisfaction with both treatment models. Pediatric patients aged 6 years and older who are seen in the clinic for overactive bladder and have failed to improve their lower urinary tract symptoms with standard urotherapy alone will be randomized to receive either parasacral TENS or oxybutynin, an oral anticholinergic medication routinely used in pediatric patients for this condition.

Patients randomized to parasacral TENS will receive a treatment plan that includes initial instructions on how to apply and use the TENS unit. The patients will perform 30-minute sessions, twice a week, for 12 weeks. A TENS unit will be loaned to the family for the duration of the treatment. This therapy will be administered at home by their guardians. Bladder diaries, the Vancouver Scoring System for Dysfunctional Elimination, and Likert scales for parental and patient preference and adherence to treatment will be administered prior to starting the study, at week 4, week 8, and upon completion of treatment to analyze the efficacy of TENS in treating pediatric overactive bladder compared to oxybutynin.

brief_summary:
Incisional hernia is a common condition after abdominal surgery and is often associated with pain, impaired physical function, and reduced quality of life. It may also be complicated by incarceration and strangulation, with the potential for acute and life-threatening events. Surgical repair is the only curative treatment, and in many cases requires complex abdominal wall reconstruction, with substantial morbidity and a risk of recurrence.

In recent years, minimally invasive laparoscopic and robot-assisted surgery has gained an increasingly important role in the treatment of ventral hernias. Retromuscular mesh placement combined with closure of the fascial defect has been developed to combine biomechanical principles from open Rives-Stoppa reconstruction with the potential benefits of minimally invasive techniques.

A key knowledge gap is which suture material should be used for defect closure: non-absorbable sutures, which provide permanent mechanical stability but leave permanent foreign material, or slowly absorbable sutures, which degrade over time and may reduce suture-related complications. In clinical practice, the choice is often driven by local tradition and surgeon preference rather than robust evidence.

Evidence from abdominal wall closure after elective laparotomy supports the use of slowly absorbable suture material; however, those results cannot be directly transferred to minimally invasive ventral hernia surgery where mesh reinforcement, biomechanics, and healing processes differ. Randomized multicenter trials specifically evaluating the impact of suture material in laparoscopic or robot-assisted retromuscular ventral/incisional hernia repair are lacking.

Against this background, the present trial compares slowly absorbable versus non-absorbable sutures in minimally invasive retromuscular incisional hernia repair, focusing on an objective long-term endpoint. CT-verified recurrence at 2 years was chosen as the primary endpoint to provide a robust and clinically meaningful measure of treatment effect. The hierarchical hypothesis framework (primary test of superiority and secondary test of non-inferiority) allows a clinically useful interpretation even if no statistically significant advantage is demonstrated.

Although incisional hernia is a subset of ventral hernias and shares pathophysiological and surgical principles with other ventral hernias, this trial is restricted to incisional hernia, where recurrence is more common and suture choice is expected to be more decisive. This restriction aims to achieve a more homogeneous study population and improve internal validity
interventions: Suturing of hernia defect with non-absorbable suture
Suturing of hernia defect with slowly absorbable suture
primary_outcomes: Primary Outcome Measure - Number of patients with a CT-verified recurrence up to 2 years after surgery
title: SUTURE TYPE AND RECURRENCE RISK AFTER INCISIONAL HERNIA REPAIR

brief_summary:
The purpose of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether, in patients with hormone receptor-positive (HR-positive) and HER2-positive advanced breast cancer whose disease has progressed after trastuzumab-based therapy, switching to pyrotinib, fulvestrant, and dalpiciclib after induction with trastuzumab rezetecan-among those without disease progression-is superior to continued treatment with trastuzumab rezetecan. The three medicines are pyrotinib (a medicine that blocks HER2 and similar signals), fulvestrant (a hormone therapy), and dalpiciclib (a medicine that slows cancer cell division).

The primary question this study aims to answer is:

Does switching to pyrotinib, fulvestrant, and dalpiciclib prolong the time participants live without their cancer worsening compared with continued treatment with trastuzumab rezetecan?

The study will also assess overall survival, tumor response to treatment, and adverse events.

Researchers will compare the three-medicine combination with continued trastuzumab rezetecan.

Participants will:

Receive trastuzumab rezetecan once every 3 weeks for 6 cycles.

If the cancer has not worsened after these 6 cycles, be randomly assigned to receive either the three-medicine combination or continued trastuzumab rezetecan.

Undergo imaging scans every 6 weeks during the first 24 weeks and every 9 weeks thereafter to assess the cancer.

Undergo blood tests, cardiac assessments, and other safety evaluations during treatment and follow-up.
lead_sponsor: Sun Yat-Sen Memorial Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University
primary_outcomes: Progression-Free Survival (PFS)
title: Trastuzumab Rezetecan Followed by Pyrotinib, Fulvestrant, and Dalpiciclib in HR-Positive, HER2-Positive Advanced Breast Cancer

brief_summary:
This research study is being conducted to determine whether a stellate ganglion block, a small injection in the neck that temporarily reduces sympathetic nervous system activity, can help reduce the risk of developing postoperative atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery.

Postoperative atrial fibrillation is a common complication after cardiac surgery and may lead to longer hospital stays and other health problems. This study is also being conducted to evaluate whether this procedure can be performed safely and feasibly in cardiac surgery patients.

The medication used in the active treatment group is bupivacaine, which is approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). However, its use as part of a stellate ganglion block for prevention of atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery is considered investigational.

The study procedure will take place after surgery while participants are in the intensive care unit (ICU), before the breathing tube is removed.

If enrolled in the study, participants will receive a single injection in the neck area while still under sedation, using ultrasound guidance, which is a type of imaging that helps the doctor see the area and place the injection safely This procedure is called a stellate ganglion block. The procedure itself takes approximately 10-15 minutes.

Before and after the procedure, the study team will perform simple measurements to assess the effect of the block. These include measuring skin temperature and checking your size. These assessments will take about 10-15 minutes.

Heart rhythm will be monitored as part of standard care during hospital stay. The study team will collect information about development atrial fibrillation within 7 days after surgery.
interventions: Stellate Ganglion Block Injection with 10 mL 0.5% Bupivacaine
Stellate Ganglion Block Injection with 10 mL Normal Saline
primary_outcomes: Success of treatment
Study Feasibility
title: SGB for Prevention of Postop A-Fib After Cardiac SurgeryTrial

brief_summary:
Continuous infusion of short-acting synthetic opioids, primarily remifentanil, is widely used for anesthesia and analgesia in ventilated patients in the intensive care unit (ICU) due to its short half-life, which is independent of hepatic or renal clearance, which may be reduced or unpredictable in these patients \[1,2\]. However, prolonged exposure results in rapid development of drug tolerance, opioid-induced hyperalgesia (OIH), and severe iatrogenic opioid withdrawal syndrome (IOWS) with abrupt discontinuation or rapid down-titration of the drug \[1-3\]. IOWS is characterized by withdrawal symptoms including delirium, restlessness, increased blood pressure, onset of sharp pain, increased respiratory and heart rates, and consequently increased metabolic demand. All of the above are undesirable and potentially dangerous in critically ill patients, and may compromise the chances of successful respiratory withdrawal in these patients \[2,4\].

To alleviate these symptoms and facilitate successful respiratory withdrawal, a long-acting opioid, such as methadone, can be used as a bridge. The use of a long-acting opioid may help prevent opioid withdrawal syndrome. Clinical protocols exist for the use of enteral methadone (oral or via gavage) for this purpose \[2,4,5\]. Methadone is a fully synthetic μ-opioid receptor agonist with high gastrointestinal bioavailability (\>80%) and a long half-life (15-60 hours) \[2,6\]. This pharmacokinetic profile provides sustained plasma concentrations that avoid the sharp troughs associated with infusion of a short-acting opiate \[5,6\]. Furthermore, methadone acts as a non-competitive antagonist at the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor \[6,7\]. By reducing central NMDA-mediated sensitization, methadone reduces OIH and attenuates acute tolerance that develops during chronic exposure to remifentanil, making it an effective pharmacological "bridger" in intensive care \[2,5,7\]. Methadone's activity at the NMDA receptor also has an analgesic effect that is not mediated through opioid receptors. Methadone is not cleared renally, so renal failure, which is common in critically ill patients, does not affect its clearance. Even in situations of hepatic insufficiency, very severe liver damage is required to have an effect on methadone clearance, an additional advantage of its use in critically ill patients. In addition, compared to other opioids (such as OxyContin or Fentanyl), methadone does not produce a significant euphoric feeling, which reduces its potential for addiction.

Although methadone is an old and well-known substance, and despite its advantages as discussed above, along with the existence of treatment protocols \[4,5\], the use of methadone in the intensive care unit remains limited due to concerns about the potential for the development of fatal cardiac arrhythmias with its use \[1,8\]. Methadone inhibits the delayed rectifier potassium current (I\_Kr) by blocking the anthraquinone-related gene (hERG) potassium channel, which may delay ventricular repolarization, prolong the corrected QT interval (QTc), and predispose patients to dangerous arrhythmias such as torsades de pointes (TdP \[1,8,9\]. Furthermore, many patients in intensive care receive other medications that may prolong the QTc interval (macrolide or fluoroquinolone antibiotics, antipsychotics for the treatment of delirium such as haloperidol or Zyprexa, gastrointestinal motility agents such as peramin or erythromycin, etc.) and/or have other disorders that may prolong the QTc interval, such as hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, or hypocalcemia.

However, current perceptions regarding Methadone-induced arrhythmias are largely derived from patients receiving methadone maintenance therapy (MMT) in outpatient settings for the treatment of chronic opioid use disorder \[1,3,8\]. These outpatient treatment groups differ substantially from critically ill patients in intensive care undergoing short-term opiate withdrawal protocols \[1,8,9\]. MMT regimens routinely use high, sometimes escalating doses of methadone (often \>100-120 mg/day) over years, these patients often take other unregulated illicit substances in addition to their "legal" methadone treatment (opioid drugs, drugs from other classes, or prescription drugs taken illegally), and these patients often have other metabolic disorders resulting from their general poor condition (malnutrition, dehydration, untreated electrolyte abnormalities, and other chronic diseases). \[1,8,9\]. In contrast, protocols for administering methadone to patients in intensive care include significantly lower doses of the drug administered for a relatively short period of time (days to weeks, in exceptional cases months, typical doses of 20-60 mg per day for most patients), patients are under continuous cardiac monitoring (ECG monitor, in some cases, as in our unit, there is also continuous monitoring of the QTc interval throughout the day), monitoring of potassium, magnesium and calcium values and clinical pharm
primary_outcomes: QTc prolongation
title: Methadone Administration in Critically Ill Patients in the Intensive Care Unit and Risk of Prolonged QTc and Cardiac Arrythmia

brief_summary:
Holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP) is an effective operation for men with urinary obstruction caused by a benign enlarged prostate. Some men leak urine for a period after the operation. Early apical release is a surgical step that frees the tip (apex) of the prostate at the start of the operation to reduce stretch on the urinary sphincter. The conventional technique cuts all the way around the apex, including the front (anterior) tissue next to the sphincter.

This randomized trial compares a modified technique, Anterior Bridge-Preserving Semicircular Early Apical Release (ABP-S-EAR), with conventional early apical release during HoLEP. ABP-S-EAR leaves the front tissue bridge between the 11 and 1 o'clock positions intact. Men aged 45 to 80 years scheduled for HoLEP at Benha University Hospital, Egypt, will be randomly assigned to one technique. The main question is whether ABP-S-EAR improves urinary continence 1 month after surgery. The trial also compares continence at 3, 6, and 12 months, operative time, bleeding, catheter time, hospital stay, urinary symptoms, urine flow, and complications.

interventions: Anterior Bridge-Preserving Semicircular Early Apical Release (ABP-S-EAR)
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants With Objective Urinary Continence at 1 Month
title: Anterior Bridge-Preserving Versus Conventional Early Apical Release During Holmium Laser Enucleation of the Prostate

brief_summary:
This study evaluated whether Cancer Patient Navigation (CPN) services could improve readiness for the transition from breast cancer diagnosis to treatment.

The study involved 64 women newly diagnosed with stage I-IIIA breast cancer who experienced high psychological distress at a cancer referral hospital in Indonesia. Participants were assigned to either a navigation group or a standard care group without randomization.

Women in the navigation group received a 30-day support program that included education about breast cancer, guidance on treatment preparation, assistance with care coordination, and emotional support. The program included three to four hospital-based sessions during scheduled visits, a patient education booklet, and online nutrition education. Women in the comparison group received standard care.

Participants' readiness to manage changes related to their cancer diagnosis and prepare for treatment was assessed before and after the study using the Measurement of Transitions in Cancer Scale.

The study aimed to determine whether women receiving navigation services experienced greater improvements in transition readiness than those receiving standard care.
primary_outcomes: Change in Health-Illness Transition Readiness
title: Cancer Patient Navigation and Readiness

brief_summary: The placement of dental implants has been a routine procedure for the rehabilitation of fully or partially edentulous patients for nearly 40 years. Dental abutments are intermediary components that connect prosthetic teeth to the implants after healing. Depending on the properties of the abutment material, plaque accumulation and bacterial adhesion may lead to inflammation and bone loss in peri-implant tissues. Developed by Nobel Biocare, the Xeal™ abutment surface protects the underlying bone, supports stable soft tissue integration, and has been shown to reduce marginal bone loss and promote healthier mucosa compared to machined abutments. However, previous studies have mostly relied on clinical and radiographic evaluations, without three-dimensional evaluation or microbiological analysis. This study aimed to evaluate peri-implant marginal bone loss (MBL), digital evaluation of peri-implant soft tissue, and differences in the microbial composition of the oral microflora colonizing the soft tissue/abutment interface between Multi-unit Abutments Xeal™ and conventional titanium multi-unit abutments placed in the posterior region.
