brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the accuracy, feasibility, and clinical usefulness of a wearable ultrasound imaging system for cardiac monitoring during perioperative care and in intensive care units (ICUs).

Traditional bedside echocardiography provides important information about heart structure and function but is usually performed intermittently. Wearable ultrasound technology may allow more frequent monitoring of cardiac function and help healthcare professionals recognize changes in patients' conditions.

This prospective device-comparison study plans to enroll 600 patients, including 400 adults and 200 children, receiving care in cardiac intensive care settings at Fuwai Hospital.

Participants will undergo cardiac monitoring using a wearable ultrasound imaging system in addition to conventional bedside echocardiography. The wearable device will obtain cardiac ultrasound images that can be transmitted wirelessly for remote assessment by physicians. Under stable clinical conditions, ultrasound assessments will generally be performed hourly, with additional assessments when significant circulatory changes occur. Conventional bedside echocardiography will be performed daily for comparison.

The study will compare measurements of cardiac structure and function obtained using the two methods, including left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and evaluate their agreement and ability to identify clinically important cardiovascular changes.

In a subgroup of 400 participants (300 adults and 100 children), wearable ultrasound images will also be displayed alongside electrocardiography, blood pressure, and oxygen saturation measurements on bedside monitors to evaluate the feasibility and potential clinical benefits of integrated monitoring.

The findings may help determine whether wearable ultrasound technology can provide accurate and practical cardiac monitoring for critically ill patients.
lead_sponsor: China National Center for Cardiovascular Diseases
primary_outcomes: Agreement in Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction Measurements
title: Wearable Ultrasound for Cardiac Monitoring During Surgery and in Intensive Care

brief_summary:
Background:

Large and giant congenital melanocytic nevi (LGCMN) are dark birthmarks (moles). They can grow to 8 inches or more across. People with LGCMN have an increased risk of getting skin cancer or problems with the nervous system. Researchers want to find out if a drug approved for a different use (mirdametinib) can shrink the size of LGCMN.

Objective:

To test mirdametinib in people with LGCMN.

Eligibility:

People aged 3 to 40 years with LGCMN.

Design:

Participants will be screened. Their LGCMN sites will be measured and photographed. They will have blood tests, an eye exam, and tests of their heart function. They will also have:

* An exam of their nervous system: Their muscle strength, ability to feel and touch, balance, alertness, and other skills will be tested.
* Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan: They will lie on a bed that slides into a tube; the scan will use large magnets to create images of their brain and spinal cord.
* Skin biopsy: A small sample of their skin may be taken.
* VECTRA scan: This is a 3-dimensional imaging system that takes pictures of all of the skin all at once.

Mirdametinib will be either pills or capsules that are taken by mouth. Participants will take the drug in 4-week cycles. They will take the pills 2 times a day for 3 weeks with 1 week off.

Participants may continue taking the drug for 2 years. They will have clinic visits 12 times while taking the drug. Imaging scans and other tests will be repeated.

Participants will continue to have checkups every 6 months for 3 more years.
conditions: Large and Giant Congenital Melanocytic Nevi
primary_outcomes: Determine whether treatment with mirdametinib results in objective decreases in the largest diameter of LGCMN
title: Mirdametinib to Reduce the Size of Large/Giant Congenital Melanocytic Nevi in Children, Adolescents and Young Adults

brief_summary:
Purpose: This multicenter, prospective, single-arm phase 2 clinical trial aims to evaluate the safety, feasibility, and clinical outcomes of the SPADE operation (Spade-Shaped Anastomosis) in patients undergoing laparoscopic or robotic proximal gastrectomy for early gastric cancer located in the upper stomach

. Background: While proximal gastrectomy (removing only the upper part of the stomach) offers nutritional advantages over total gastrectomy, it often leads to significant postoperative reflux esophagitis

* The SPADE technique was developed to prevent this by creating an artificial anti-reflux mechanism (angle of His and pseudo-fornix) using double suture anchoring between the esophagus and the stomach

Study Plan:

Participants: The study will enroll approximately 159 patients with tumors (size ≤ 4 cm) located in the upper third of the stomach who are eligible for gastric function-preserving surgery . Intervention: All participants will undergo laparoscopic or robotic proximal gastrectomy followed by the SPADE reconstruction method

. Primary Objective: The primary goal is to determine the incidence of endoscopic reflux esophagitis at one year postoperatively

. Secondary Objectives: Investigators will also monitor postoperative reflux symptoms, nutritional parameters (such as weight, hemoglobin, and vitamin B12 levels), surgical complications, quality of life, and 3-year survival rates

. Hypothesis: The researchers hypothesize that the SPADE operation is a safe and effective surgical approach that can provide equivalent reflux prevention (a target rate of approximately 2.9%) compared to existing complex reconstruction methods, while maintaining the benefits of preserving gastric function
interventions: Spade-Shaped Anastomosis after Laparoscopic or Robotic Proximal Gastrectomy Using Double Suture Anchoring between the Posterior Wall of the Esophagus and the Anterior Wall of the Stomac
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Endoscopic Reflux Esophagitis at 1 Year
title: SPADE Clinical Trial.

brief_summary:
Healthy aging requires effective, accessible, and sustainable interventions capable of preserving functional capacity and preventing age-related decline. In this context, walking football has emerged as a safe, inclusive physical exercise modality with high adherence among older adults, demonstrating benefits for muscle health, metabolic profile, and psychosocial well-being. On the other hand, creatine monohydrate supplementation is backed by robust scientific evidence as a strategy to enhance exercise adaptations, promote muscle mass maintenance, and improve factors related to metabolic syndrome.

The objective of this project is to evaluate the effects of creatine supplementation combined with regular walking football practice on muscle quality and metabolic profile in older adults, as well as to explore the underlying biological mechanisms using a cell culture-based experimental model. The ultimate goal is to determine the potential of this intervention to promote healthy longevity through functional, muscular, and metabolic indicators associated with healthspan.

Specifically, the study will analyze the intervention's effects on body composition, physical fitness, and metabolic syndrome markers; evaluate its impact on psychosocial well-being, quality of life, and cognitive function; and investigate the molecular mechanisms related to muscle health, protection against oxidative stress, and the modulation of senescence using an ex vivo/in vitro model.

The project will be carried out in two complementary phases. First, a longitudinal experimental study will be conducted in older adults participating in walking football programs and supplemented with creatine. Subsequently, skeletal muscle cultures will be exposed to conditioned sera obtained before and after the intervention to investigate its biological effects.

This approach will integrate the evaluation of clinical efficacy with the study of the underlying mechanisms, generating applicable knowledge for designing personalized, sustainable, and cost-effective strategies to prevent sarcopenia and metabolic syndrome.
interventions: Monohydrate Creatine supplementation during Walking Football training
primary_outcomes: Muscle Quality
title: Creatine and Muscle Health in Madrid's Walking Footballers.

brief_summary: This study examined whether a single 120-minute, therapist-led Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (SS-ACT) session, delivered individually and face-to-face in Urdu, was associated with reduced generalized anxiety symptoms among undergraduate students in Pakistan. Fifty full-time undergraduate students aged 18 to 25 at GIFT University (25 male, 25 female), who scored 5 or above on the GAD-7 and met DSM-5 criteria for generalized anxiety disorder on the SCID-5 interview, received the session. Anxiety symptoms (GAD-7) were measured before the session, immediately after it, and at a two-week follow-up. Psychological inflexibility (AAQ-II) was measured before and immediately after the session. The study also examined whether changes in anxiety differed between male and female participants. This was a single-group study without a control or comparison group.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to is to learn whether adding EEG neurofeedback (NFB) to repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) is safe and feasible for adults with major depressive disorder (MDD). The study will also explore whether combining NFB with TMS may improve depression symptoms and change brain activity related to mood, focus, and rumination. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is alpha-down neurofeedback safe, tolerable, and feasible for people with MDD?
* Does alpha-down neurofeedback improve symptoms of depression, anxiety, and difficulties with attention, emotion regulation, and rumination?
* Does combining neurofeedback with TMS produce greater changes in symptoms than either treatment alone?

Researchers will compare 3 groups (TMS only, neurofeedback only, and TMS combined with neurofeedback) to see if combining neurofeedback with TMS will produce greater changes in symptoms than either treatment alone.

Participants will:

* Complete assessments of depression severity, anxiety, and cognitive function.
* Complete 5 treatment sessions Monday through Friday.
* Receive alpha-down neurofeedback, TMS, or both, depending on their group assignment.
* Complete EEG recordings of brain activity before and after treatment.
* Complete a questionnaire about their experience in the study.
primary_outcomes: Feasibility and Tolerability of NFB and rTMS Interventions
title: Effect of Neurofeedback and TMS

brief_summary:
The overall study goal is to test the efficacy and cost-effectiveness of Sleeping Healthy, Living Healthy (SHLH), a novel intervention that combines healthy sleep practices with mind-body integrative health (MBIH) approaches to improve sleep health among urban adolescents. The study will also use a mixed-methods multi-stakeholder process evaluation to understand barriers and facilitators to adoption and implementation of SHLH across geographically diverse high schools, and to inform future dissemination and scale-up efforts.

Aim #1: To evaluate the efficacy of SHLH in 294 urban adolescents with lower than recommended sleep duration for age. The study will randomize students from 12 NYC public high schools over 3 years, following them at four timepoints for 1-year post-intervention. While adolescents are the primary respondent for all outcomes, caregivers will be interviewed at the same intervals. School attendance data and grades will be obtained from schools.

Aim #2: To assess the cost-effectiveness of SHLH compared to an attention control sleep intervention from the school system and societal perspectives. Outcomes will be cost per day of school absences and tardiness avoided (school system perspective) and cost per quality-adjusted life year (QALY) gained (societal perspective).

Aim #3: To track the extent of uptake and delivery of SHLH across students and schools, and to identify multi-level factors that influence the implementation of SHLH, with the goal of informing future dissemination and scale-up of SHLH.
primary_outcomes: PROMIS Sleep-Related Impairment (SRI) t-score
Average length of sleep duration
title: SHLH for Urban Adolescents (Efficacy Trial)

brief_summary:
The World Health Organization defines quality of life as "a state of physical, mental, and social well-being"; therefore, it is important to consider the patient holistically, taking into account social function and the ability to meet basic needs, such as the ability to eat and pain control.

In this context, oral health plays a key role in patient well-being, as it is essential for communication, chewing, nutrition, and aesthetics.

The loss of teeth-whether extracted due to periodontal disease or caries-can cause masticatory, phonetic, and aesthetic impairments, which are considered factors contributing to a decline in quality of life.

The loss of natural teeth compromises masticatory function, making appropriate prosthetic rehabilitation essential to restore oral function and improve quality of life.

brief_summary:
1\. Brief Summary This prospective observational study aims to evaluate the 6-month longitudinal changes in chronic pain, pain characteristics, coping strategies, and functional performance in children and adolescents aged 7 to 18 years diagnosed with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD), with a primary focus on comparing ambulatory and non-ambulatory disease stages.

Pediatric DMD patients followed at the University of Health Sciences Antalya Training and Research Hospital Neuromuscular Diseases Center will undergo comprehensive evaluations at baseline (Month 0) and at 6 months follow-up (Month 6). Pain parameters will be evaluated using the Adolescent Pediatric Pain Tool (APPT) to assess pain intensity, body localization, and sensory/affective/evaluative/temporal qualities, and the Brief Pain Inventory (BPI) 7-item Pain Interference Scale to determine pain interference with daily activities. Pain coping strategies will be assessed using the Pediatric Pain Coping Inventory (PPCI, adolescent and parent versions). Functional and motor assessments will include the North Star Ambulatory Assessment (NSAA), 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT), stair climb/descend tests, Vignos and Brooke scales, handgrip dynamometry, manual muscle testing (MMT), and range of motion (ROM) and contracture evaluations, alongside anthropometrics and quality of life.

The central hypotheses are that non-ambulatory patients experience chronic pain more frequently, with longer duration, greater intensity, and across a higher number of anatomical sites than ambulatory patients. Furthermore, the study hypothesizes that anatomical pain sites, pain-aggravating and pain-relieving factors, and pain coping mechanisms differ significantly between ambulatory and non-ambulatory stages.
interventions: Routine Clinical Follow-up and Pain Assessment
primary_outcomes: Change in Chronic Pain Intensity From Baseline to 6 Months
title: Does Chronic Pain Change Over Time in Children With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy?

brief_summary: This retrospective study evaluates the functional impact of individualized multisite neuro-orthopedic upper limb surgery in children with unilateral cerebral palsy (hemiplegic CP). Using a before-and-after design in which each patient serves as their own control, the study analyzes data collected in routine clinical care up to 3-5 years before and 1-2 years after surgery. The primary outcome is upper limb function as measured by the Modified Melbourne Assessment (MA2), which assesses range of motion and dexterity. Secondary outcomes include unimanual precision and fluidity (MA2), global manual dexterity (Box and Block Test), bimanual performance (Assisting Hand Assessment), and patient/parent satisfaction. Approximately 70 patients operated at the Centre Médico-Chirurgical de Réadaptation des Massues between January 2012 and June 2025 will be included. The study also aims to identify factors influencing surgical outcomes, such as age at surgery, associated cognitive or sensory impairments, and adherence to post-operative orthotic protocols.

primary_outcomes: Upper Limb Range of Motion and Dexterity - Modified Melbourne Assessment (MA2)
title: Functional Benefits of Multisite Upper Limb Surgery in Children With Unilateral Cerebral Palsy (RETRO-CHIRc)

brief_summary: This randomised controlled trial compares three supraglottic airway devices (laryngeal masks) in children with a body weight of 3-30 kg undergoing elective surgery under general anaesthesia: the SaCoVLM video laryngeal mask (UE Medical), which has an integrated camera allowing visual confirmation and adjustment of mask position, the LMA Supreme (Teleflex) and the Ambu AuraGain (Ambu). Children are randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to one of the three devices. The main question is whether the SaCoVLM provides a higher oropharyngeal leak pressure (a measure of how well the mask seals the airway) than the LMA Supreme and the Ambu AuraGain. Secondary questions include first-attempt insertion success, the need for repositioning or reinsertion of the mask during surgery and airway-related complications.

brief_summary: Insomnia is common among people living with HIV and is linked to fatigue and lower quality of life. Cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is the recommended first-line treatment, but access is limited in Indonesia. This study develops a nurse-led sleep coaching programme based on CBT-I principles and delivered online (telenursing), and tests whether the programme and the study procedures are feasible. Fifty adults living with HIV who have insomnia symptoms will complete two baseline assessments four weeks apart, four weekly online coaching sessions and a follow-up assessment four weeks after the last session. The study measures recruitment, retention, attendance, adherence, data completeness, fidelity, usability and safety, and describes changes in sleep, fatigue, pain, anxiety and depression.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine whether adding a posterior pericapsular deep-gluteal (PPD) block to pericapsular nerve group (PENG) and lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (LFCN) blocks improves pain control after total hip arthroplasty.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does adding a posterior pericapsular deep-gluteal block reduce clinically significant pain during movement in the early postoperative period?
* Does adding this block reduce postoperative pain and opioid requirements?
* Does adding this block improve functional recovery after surgery?

Researchers will compare patients receiving PENG and LFCN blocks with patients receiving PENG and LFCN blocks plus a posterior pericapsular deep-gluteal block to determine whether blocking the posterior region of the hip provides additional pain relief.

Participants will:

* Receive ultrasound-guided nerve blocks before surgery according to their assigned study group.
* Undergo total hip arthroplasty under spinal anesthesia.
* Have their pain assessed at predefined times after surgery, including during movement.
* Be evaluated for opioid requirements and functional recovery after surgery.
primary_outcomes: 6-hour dynamic pain intensity
title: Posterior Pericapsular Deep-gluteal Block

Participants will take their assigned product once daily and complete self-reported questionnaires at Baseline, Week 4, Week 8, and Week 12. brief_summary:
Investigational Device

* TSK-001 injectable glucose-functionalised gold nanoparticle solution for intratumoural administration (0.3 mg nanoparticles in 1mL water for injection)
* Laser device 808 nm

Dose regimen TSK-001

* Part 1: Single intratumoural injection at 10%, 15%, and 20% of the tumour volume (vol/vol).
* Part 2: Two intratumoural injections at the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) or maximum administered dose (MAD) administered two weeks apart.
* Part 3: Two injections of TSK-001 at the Recommended Phase 2 Dose (RP2D) administered 2 weeks apart.

Laser Device

Near-infra red (NIR) irradiation of the tumour will be performed 1 hour after each injection of TSK-001 at the following laser settings:

* Wavelength: 808 nm
* Power density: 1 Watt Mode: Continuous wave
* Duration: 10 minutes

Comparator N/A

Treatment Groups Part 1:

Part 1 consists of 3 single dose escalation cohorts:

* Cohort 1: TSK-001 10% vol/vol
* Cohort 2: TSK-001 15% vol/vol
* Cohort 3: TSK-001 20% vol/vol

Part 2:

Part 2 consists of a multiple dose expansion cohort who will receive two injections of TSK-001 at the MAD or MTD administered 2 weeks apart.

Part 3:

Part 3 consists of a Phase 2 multiple dose cohort who will receive two injections of TSK-001 at the RP2D administered 2 weeks apart.

Objectives Primary Objectives Part 1 To assess the safety and tolerability of a single administration of TSK001 combined with NIR irradiation in patients with nodular Basal Cell Carcinoma (nBCC).

Part 2 To assess the safety and tolerability of two administrations of TSK-001 combined with NIR irradiation in patients with nBCC.

Part 3 To assess Complete Response (CR) (disappearance of cutaneous tumour) of the target lesion using RECIST v1.1 criteria following two administrations of TSK-001 combined with NIR irradiation in patients with nBCC.

Secondary Objectives Part 1

* To assess the pharmacokinetics (PK) of TSK-001 in plasma and urine, and gold concentration in tumour following a single administration of TSK-001 combined with NIR irradiation in patients with nBCC.
* To assess Complete Response (CR) (disappearance of cutaneous tumour) of the target lesion using RECIST v1.1 criteria following single administration of TSK-001 combined with NIR irradiation in patients with nBCC.
* To assess complete clinical and imaging clearance through photography and lack of diagnostic structures on dermoscopy

Part2

* To assess the pharmacokinetics (PK) of TSK-001 in plasma and urine, and gold concentration in tumour following two treatments (14 days apart) of TSK-001 combined with NIR irradiation in patients with nBCC.
* To assess Complete Response (CR) (disappearance of cutaneous tumour) of the target lesion using RECIST v1.1 criteria following two administrations of TSK-001 combined with NIR irradiation in patients with nBCC.
* To assess complete clinical and imaging clearance through photography and lack of diagnostic structures on dermoscopy.

Part 3:

* To assess complete clinical and imaging clearance through photography and lack of diagnostic structures on dermoscopy.
* To assess the scar healing effect of TSK-001 combined with NIR irradiation in patients with BCC.
* To assess the safety and tolerability of two administrations of TSK001 combined with NIR irradiation in patients with nBCC.
* To assess the gold concentration in tumour following two administrations of TSK-001 combined with NIR irradiation in patients with nBCC.

Endpoints Primary endpoints Parts 1 and 2

* Incidence, severity, and relationship of adverse events (AEs).
* Changes from baseline in clinical laboratory parameters, vital signs, and 12-lead ECG.
* Incidence, frequency and severity of local skin reactions (LSRs), pigmentation and scarring using the LSR Grading Scale.
* Pain using a 100 mm Visual Analogic Scale (VAS)
* Lesion temperature measured by infrared thermography

Part 3:

* CR, defined as the disappearance of the target tumour lesion according to RECIST v1.1 at Day 29.
* Histology of excised residual tumour from Day 29 to Day 180.
* Histology of tumour in punch biopsy at Day 180 at the latest for observation of any residual viable tumour cells after treatment.

Secondary endpoints Part 1

* Plasma and urine PK parameters
* Presence of gold nanoparticles in excised residual tumour at Day 29.
* CR, defined as the disappearance of the target tumour lesion according to RECIST v1.1 at Day 29
